If no key can be made: write `unavailable` **with the session** and try again when the boot or the macOS version changed, after 7 days — or at once in any **other session** (§17.29): the failure is that session's. `gclone status` says "no Secure Enclave on this machine" only when a session with graphic access could not make a key, and otherwise "no Secure Enclave key could be made in session 0x2 (without graphic access) on <date>"; the trial that later starts in a session that can make one keeps the earlier failure as a `failures` entry, so it is not "complete" before somebody looked (`--new-trial`). **The same holds for what was recorded after a move had ended a trial** (0.5.1, §17.30; `Record::carried`): a login that could not seal writes `unavailable` into the ended record (the device had been broken in a session the trial never saw, and its owner signed in again from there — to the plain file), a call that did not return writes a failure; the trial that starts on that device afterwards begins with them, `status` warns, and nothing is moved a second time before somebody looked. What the old key itself failed at before its move stays with the old key. The step works in two halves: the enclave calls on the record as it was read, without a lock; then the result is written into the record as it is by then (`trial::update`), and dropped if another process changed the trial's key in between.
2. A record with a key → open the test value (one enclave call, 4–6 ms) and compare it with `canary_hash`. Success → add an `ok` entry if this (day, boot, session) has none; most runs write nothing. Failure → add it to `failures` and count it, with the result of a fresh-key probe.
3. **A step that does not return** (§17.29): after two seconds the command goes on; the record gets a failure with `timed_out` ("the call into the Secure Enclave did not return within 2 s"), and the same boot and session are left alone for a day, so that it is one slow command and not every command. The thread ends with the process. Nobody has seen the real framework block — the stand-in's `hang` mode shows that nothing in gclone bounded it; the sessions nobody measured (ssh, a LaunchDaemon, before the first unlock) are where it would.

What `gclone status` and `gclone keystore` show from it: days with a success; **survived a restart** = an `ok` entry whose `boot` differs from `created_boot` (a clock jump is not a restart); the sessions seen, as "with graphic access" / "without" and the raw word; the failures. **Complete** (the trial has passed) = at least 3 days **whose newest success is at least 48 hours after the first** (`trial::MIN_AGE_MS`: `last_ok_ms − created_ms`; 0.5.1, §17.30 — three UTC dates alone can be 23:59, the next day and 00:01, little more than 24 hours), a restart survived, and no failure. `status` reads "3 days, not yet 48 hours apart" in between. A failure never clears by itself: `gclone keystore check --new-trial` starts a new key and record, which has to pass in full. The evidence belongs to the key the device will depend on: every move seals the secrets **to the trial's own key** when its test value opens at that moment (one enclave key seals any number of values). When the trial's test value does **not** open at the moment of `keystore use enclave` (or of a login), the secrets are sealed to a new key, the command says that the trial has no evidence for it — and so does every later look (§17.29): `gclone keystore` reads "ended at the move — the secrets were sealed to a NEW key made then; the trial's evidence (…) belongs to another key", `status` and `keystore` warn (the warning names `gclone keystore check --new-trial`, which forgets the record), `--json` has `trial.key_holds_secrets: false`. **Only where there was evidence to mistake** (0.5.1, §17.30): a trial that ended on its first day without a restart — what `keystore use enclave` as the first command after a login left with 0.5.0 — reads "none for the key that holds the secrets (a trial that had only begun ended when they were sealed)" and warns about nothing; and only for the sealing that ended the trial: a later one to another key forgets the record (above). After a move the record stays, with `moved_ms` and without `key` and `canary`; a record without a key on a device that is on `secrets.json` again starts a new key and record.

**The automatic move** (0.5.1, §17.30; `keystore::automatic_move`, called from `LayeredStore::after_load`). The first run that loads the secrets after the trial has passed moves them into `secrets.sealed` — with no command, no passphrase and no question.

*When.* All of these, looked at in this order by the run that just took its step of the trial:
1. the device's secrets were answered from `secrets.json`, and it holds keys;
2. the opt-outs are off: the choice is not `file`, `keystore.json` is readable, `GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0` is not set and has left no marker (`keystore-trial.off`), and this process has a sealer;
3. the step of this run **came back within its two seconds** (a step that did not is a recorded failure, and no move follows);
4. the trial's record **is complete**: the test value opened on at least 3 days that are 48 hours apart, in a boot other than the one the key was made in, and no failure is on it — of any session, at any time;
5. **this process opens the test value once more, now, with the record's key** (rule 6): a process in a session that cannot use the key moves nothing — and its step has just recorded the failure that stops everybody else;
6. under the lock (one try, no wait: a busy lock means another gclone is moving or signing in, and a later run looks again): `secrets.json` is byte for byte what was read before, still holds keys, **the opt-outs are still off**, and a `secrets.sealed` beside it — what a move leaves that was killed after its rename — opens here, holds the same keys **and is sealed to the very key this move seals to** (0.5.1, §17.30: an interrupted automatic move always is, because the trial's record ends only after the plain file is gone). A sealed file beside it that does not open, holds other keys, or is sealed to another key stops the move: it may be the only copy of another state — or the store of an earlier sealing, beside which an older gclone has since signed in — and only the owner's command (`keystore use`) settles it; `status` says so, and the run before this point has not even taken a step of the trial ("The trial", above).

*How.* `keystore::move_to_enclave(…, MoveBy::Trial)`: the one move sequence, steps (1)–(4), (6) and (7) of `keystore use enclave` below — seal the exact bytes to the trial's key, open the ciphertext in memory, write `secrets.sealed`, read it back strictly and through the enclave, and only then remove `secrets.json`, `fsync` the directory, and end the trial's record. Two differences from the command: **`keystore.json` is not written** (the choice is the owner's), and in its place, before the plain file goes, **the note is owed** (`keystore-note.due`, created with `O_EXCL`). **The note is a condition of the move** (0.5.1, §17.30): if the marker can neither be created nor is there already as a file — a disk with one free block took the sealed file and the record and had no room for it — the sealed file of this run is removed again, `secrets.json` stays, and a later run tries again; otherwise nobody would ever be told that the device now depends on this Mac's enclave and on the passphrase. What the command does before its move — proving the key against the vault, checking the passphrase against a keyfile, asking — is not done: the move changes nothing about the secrets, and it must not need the network or a person.

*The bar: three days, a restart, no failure — kept as 0.5.0 had it for its advice.* The bar exists so that a device that works today from the plain file, with whatever runs unattended on it, is never broken by a store that stops opening. What each part is for: **the restart** is the one thing no test inside one process can show, and it was not measured for §17.28 (Apple documents the key's representation as the way to restore the key on the same device later; each Mac now shows it for itself before anything depends on it). **The days** stand for "what runs on this Mac has run": a daily schedule comes around at least twice in three days, a run in a session where the key does not open leaves a failure, and one failure stops the move for good. **"Three days" are three UTC dates whose first and last success are at least 48 hours apart** (0.5.1, §17.30): three dates alone can be 23:59, the next day and 00:01 of the day after — the stand-in showed a move 1442 minutes after the trial began — and in 24 hours a daily job runs once at best; in 48 hours it runs twice. A trial that 0.5.0 began carries `created_ms`, so nothing about it starts over. **No failure, ever** rather than "more successes than failures": a session that fails once is a session that would be broken. Shortening was considered and rejected: the device has been on the plain file for as long as it has been connected, so two more days change little about what a copy of the file is worth, while each day less is a day less for a scheduled session to show up; and every Mac that ran 0.5.0 has days on its record already (the record's format is unchanged, so a 0.5.0 trial that is complete is followed by the move at the first run of this version). Lengthening would not cover a weekly job either. **The bar is zero for a login** — a new device, or one whose sealed store was already what it depended on: nothing that ran before can break, the owner is at the keyboard with the passphrase, and the in-process round trip is the test. **Which logins those are** (0.5.1, §17.30; `LayeredStore::key_for_login`): the trial's record is absent, or ended with a move (the device depended on the enclave already) and holds nothing recorded since. **Not** a login on a device that works from a keyed `secrets.json` (the end of a login leaves it alone), **not** one on a signed-out device whose trial is running and has not passed — the device was working from the plain file a `gclone logout` ago, with its unattended jobs, and the trial had not yet seen a restart or all of them: such a login goes to `secrets.json`, the trial goes on, and it decides — and **not** one where the record holds a failure. A trial that has passed and was not followed by its move yet (the device was signed out in between) lends a login its key if its test value opens in that process, and otherwise the login stays on the plain file, as rule 6 has it for the move. The choice `enclave` overrides all of this: it is the owner's command. What the bar cannot show, and what then happens: a session that never ran during the trial (a weekly job, ssh) and cannot use the enclave gets the text "The Secure Enclave cannot be used in this session … `gclone keystore use file` — from a session where it works — moves the secrets back to the plain file", exit 4; a key that dies later (the Mac replaced, a restore) gets "This Mac's Secure Enclave cannot open this device's sealed key … Run `gclone login`". Neither is a dead end; both are an unattended job that fails until its owner looks.

*Time.* The move runs on a thread of its own; the command waits for it for at most ten seconds (two enclave calls of a few milliseconds and a handful of small writes; `AUTO_MOVE_WAIT`). A move that takes longer goes on while the command does its work — every point of it is a safe place to be cut off (the crash table) — and the trial's record gets a failure with `timed_out`, so that it is not tried again run after run.

*The note*, once, to a person (stderr is a terminal, no `-q`, no `--json`): when the move happens in such a run, at once; otherwise it is owed and shown by the next such run that finds the device on `secrets.sealed` alone — whoever removes `keystore-note.due` shows it. `gclone keystore use file`, `gclone keystore use enclave`, `logout`, the first save of a login on a signed-out device and the move at the end of a login remove the marker unshown (0.5.1, §17.30: each of them says itself what it did, or has nothing left to say it about; gclone 0.5.0 and older do not know the marker, and their `logout` leaves it). ▸ *"note: this device's login and vault key are now kept in secrets.sealed, which only this Mac's Secure Enclave can open (gclone tested it over several days and a restart first); the plain secrets.json is gone. A copy of the sealed file is useless anywhere else. If this Mac is erased, repaired or replaced, `gclone login` and your passphrase connect it again. `gclone keystore use file` moves back to the plain file (gclone 0.4.0 and older read only that one); `gclone keystore` shows the details."*

*Concurrency.* Readers take no lock and see `secrets.json` until it is removed, `secrets.sealed` from then on (§8.3). Of several processes that find the trial passed at once, one gets the lock and moves; the others find the lock busy or the plain file gone and do nothing. A `login` that saves at the same moment either comes first — the move then sees other bytes than it read and stops — or second, and finds the sealed store.

**`GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0`, for the whole device** (0.5.1, §17.30; `keystore::mark_trial_off`). The variable in a run's environment says "this run must not come to depend on the Secure Enclave" — a scheduler's job in a session nobody tried. In the process that carries it: no step of the trial, no move, no sealing login (unless the choice is `enclave`). That alone did not keep the promise: it made the one session its owner was unsure about the one session the test never saw, any other run passed the bar and removed `secrets.json`, and the job needed the enclave after all (shown with the stand-in: a job that set the variable every day in a session that cannot open anything failed with exit 4 from the day a terminal's run moved the secrets, and the trial's record never held a failure). So **a run with the variable that is answered from a `secrets.json` with keys** — on a Mac with a sealer, the choice not `file` — **leaves the empty marker `keystore-trial.off`** (`O_EXCL`, once), and while it is there **no run of the device takes a step of the trial, seals a login or moves anything**; the move looks at it again under the lock. `status` and `keystore` say "kept: a run with GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0 uses this device"; `--json` has `trial_off_marker`. **`gclone keystore use enclave`** (the owner's word against it: the move, and on a sealed device the settling of step 6) **and `gclone keystore check --new-trial` remove it**; a run with the variable puts it back. `logout` leaves it, like the choice. It never un-seals: a sealed store is read with the variable set like any other, and such a run leaves no marker. What it cannot do: a job that has carried the variable since 0.5.0 left no marker then, so a Mac whose trial had already passed is moved by the first run of 0.5.1 that does not carry it — the upgrade notes in `docs/SECURITY.md` say to run the job, or `gclone keystore use file`, first.

**`gclone keystore use enclave [--passphrase-file F] [--skip-passphrase-check] [--all-keyfiles] [--yes]`.** Refused with the reason on Linux, in a debug build without a test sealer, in a session where no enclave key can be made, on a device that is not connected, and where `secrets.json` holds no keys ("run `gclone login` first"; this includes a keyless `secrets.json` beside the sealed file). Without a terminal and without `--yes` it stops with a usage error before anything else.
0. **The trial's step of this run, and nothing more** (0.5.1; `LayeredStore::without_unasked_move`): the secrets are loaded once with the automatic move switched off. Without the step the command picked a new key, the load of step 2 started a trial with *another* key, and step 5 closed that trial's record: `status` and `keystore` then warned for good that the secrets were "sealed to a key that was made at the move … the trial's evidence belongs to another key" — about a trial that had no evidence (§17.30; `gclone keystore use enclave` as the first command after a login, or after `keystore check`, which stores nothing). **Not the whole of what a load does elsewhere**: as first built, this step also made the automatic move on a device whose trial had passed — before step 2 had proven the key and before step 3 had checked the passphrase — after which the command found the device sealed, said "Nothing was moved", and exited 0 with a wrong passphrase. The move of this command is step 5, after its checks, on every device.
1. **The key** (cheap, before the network; `keystore::pick_key`): the trial's key if its test value opens now, else a new key — made, reloaded, public halves compared, a probe sealed and opened.
2. **Open the vault** like `passwd` (`open_ctx`, exclusive state lock, refresh required). This proves the login and the cached keys against the store.
3. **Check the way back.** List the keyfiles on the store; none → stop: "run `gclone passwd` first". Ask for the passphrase (terminal, or `--passphrase-file`) and run the unlock that `login` uses on a new device (`login::unlock_with_passphrase`: the candidates, the bounds and the question about older keyfiles of §2.6). The keyring it yields must equal the cached one. Wrong passphrase → stop, nothing changed: "Not sure of the passphrase? `gclone passwd` on this device sets a new one now, without the old one." `--skip-passphrase-check` skips this step with a warning.
4. **Say what will change and ask** (`--yes` answers): the trial's evidence and what it has not seen (fewer than 3 days, no restart, no session without graphic access, failures); "If this Mac is erased or repaired, the passphrase you just entered is the only way back for this device."; that older gclone binaries on this Mac will say "not signed in", that their `logout` will not sign the device out and that a running `gclone web` or `serve restic` of an older version stops — restic starts `gclone` from its `PATH` — followed by every other file named `gclone` on `PATH` and in `~/.local/bin`, `~/.nix-profile/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` and `/opt/homebrew/bin` (listed, never started); "Run `gclone keystore check` from your scheduler if gclone runs there."
5. **Move** (`keystore::move_to_enclave(…, MoveBy::Command)` — the sequence that the automatic move and the end of a login share), under the exclusive secrets lock (wait up to 5 s): (1) read `secrets.json` strictly again; its bytes `B` must be the ones the command read before step 2, else stop: "the login changed meanwhile, run the command again" — unless `secrets.json` is gone and `secrets.sealed` opens here: another `keystore use enclave` finished first, which is said as that (`MoveError::AlreadySealed`, exit 0; §17.29); (2) `C = seal(P, B)`; open `C` in memory, it must equal `B`; (3) write `secrets.sealed` with `write_atomic` and compare the file's bytes; (4) read it back through the normal load path (strict file read, enclave open); it must give `B`; (5) write `keystore.json` with `enclave` and remove the markers `keystore-trial.off` and `keystore-note.due` (the command only; the automatic move owes its note here instead — and stops if it cannot — and the move at the end of a login writes no choice and removes the owed note); (6) remove `secrets.json` and its temp leftovers; `fsync` the directory; (7) the trial's record, if there is one (`trial::note_sealed`): a running trial ends — rewritten without `key` and `canary`, with `moved_ms` —, and the record of a trial that ended at an earlier sealing, for another key, is forgotten. A failure in (2)–(4) removes the `secrets.sealed` of this run and leaves `secrets.json`: nothing changed.
6. Print where the secrets are now and how to go back. If the device is on `secrets.sealed` alone already, the command verifies that it opens, says so, and **settles what an interrupted command left** (`keystore::settle_sealed`, under the lock; §17.29): plain temp copies of the secrets are removed, and a `keystore.json` that still says `file` — an interrupted `use file` — says `enclave` again, so that the next login after a logout is not saved to the plain file; on a device that was sealed by a login or by itself (no choice on file) the command records `enclave` and says just that; the marker `keystore-trial.off` goes.

**`gclone keystore use file [--discard-sealed]`** (`keystore::move_to_file`; no vault and no passphrase are needed). **It is the opt-out, and it is remembered** (0.5.1): with `file` in `keystore.json` there is no trial, no automatic move and no sealing login — the automatic move reads the choice under the same lock, so the two cannot cross — until `gclone keystore use enclave`. It also removes the marker of an owed note about a move.

| found | steps |
|---|---|
| `secrets.sealed` alone, opens | lock; write `keystore.json` with `file` **first**; write `secrets.json` (`write_atomic`, 0600) from the sealed document; read it back strictly and compare; remove `secrets.sealed`. |
| `secrets.json`, no `secrets.sealed` | lock; write the choice. Nothing moves. |
| `secrets.json` with keys, and `secrets.sealed` | lock; if the sealed file opens and its keyring equals the plain one: write the choice, remove it. If it opens with **another** keyring, or does not open: stop and say which, nothing changed — `--discard-sealed` then writes the choice and removes it (`secrets.json` is what the device has been using). |
| `secrets.json` keyless, and `secrets.sealed` opens | lock; the merged view of the load table (same guard) → write the choice; write `secrets.json` from it; read back; remove `secrets.sealed`. Not mergeable → stop, nothing changed. |
| `secrets.sealed` does not open, and `secrets.json` is absent or keyless | stop: nothing can be moved; the text of the load error. `--discard-sealed` does not remove the only copy of a key. |
| neither | write the choice (the next `login` saves to `secrets.json`). |

**Crash points.** Every write is `write_atomic`, and the new file exists before the old one is removed:

| killed | left behind | next |
|---|---|---|
| `use enclave` or the automatic move, before the rename of `secrets.sealed` | `secrets.json`, a temp file | `logout`, the next `use`, the next save of a `login` or the next move removes the temp file. After the automatic move's: the next run moves. |
| any write of `secrets.json`, before its rename | a **plain** temp copy `.secrets.json.tmp-<16 hex>` — beside a sealed store too | the same; until then `gclone status` and `gclone keystore` **count it and warn** (`plain_leftovers`; beside a sealed store: "a copy of the state folder is NOT worthless elsewhere while they are there"), §17.29 |
| `use enclave`, between that rename and the removal of `secrets.json` | both files, equal; the choice may or may not be written | readers use `secrets.json`; `status`: "an interrupted move … `gclone keystore use file` or `gclone keystore use enclave` settles it". The command again completes; the automatic move does **only if** the sealed file is sealed to the key of the trial that is running (the command had picked the trial's key), the trial has passed and the opt-outs are off — otherwise nothing finishes it by itself, no step of the trial is taken meanwhile, and `status` says "kept: nothing is tested or moved while secrets.sealed lies beside it". |
| the automatic move, between that rename and the removal of `secrets.json` | both files, equal; no choice; the note owed or not yet | readers use `secrets.json`; **the next run finishes the move** (its condition 6 accepts a sealed copy of the same keys under the trial's key), and the note is owed once — and is not shown, nor used up, while `secrets.json` is still there |
| the automatic move, after the removal of `secrets.json`, before the trial's record ends | `secrets.sealed`; the note owed; a record that still holds the trial's key | the device is sealed and working; the first load ends the record (`end_trial_of_sealing_key`: the record's `public` equals the sealed file's); until then `gclone keystore` reads the two files and reports "ended: its key holds the secrets" all the same |
| `login`, between a save to `secrets.json` and the move at its end | `secrets.json` with keys | the device works from the plain file; the trial starts, and the automatic move follows it |
| `use file`, after the choice, before `secrets.json` | `secrets.sealed`; choice `file` | the device is still sealed and working; `status` says the choice and the store differ |
| `use file`, between `secrets.json` and the removal of `secrets.sealed` | both files, equal; choice `file` | readers use `secrets.json`; `use file` again removes the sealed copy |
| `login`, between its save to `secrets.json` and the removal of `secrets.sealed` | `secrets.json` with keys, and `secrets.sealed` | readers use `secrets.json`; the next `login` or `use` removes the sealed file |

There is no instant at which neither a readable `secrets.json` nor an openable `secrets.sealed` exists, and no rename that moves the only copy away. An interrupted `use file` is never undone by a later command — nor by the automatic move: the choice is written first.

**What works where** (measured on macOS 27.2, Apple silicon, FileVault on; §17.28):

| started from | `file` | `enclave` |
|---|---|---|
| a terminal on the Mac; a LaunchAgent (`gui/<uid>`); cron | yes | yes (measured) |
| ssh, a LaunchDaemon with `UserName`, `user/<uid>` agents | yes | expected yes; **not measured** — the trial and `keystore check` find out |
| the screen locked | yes | yes by the key's class; not measured |
| after a restart, before the first login, FileVault on | nothing runs: the data volume is locked | the same |
| after a restart, before the first login, FileVault off | yes | expected no, until the first login; not measured. Such a Mac should stay on `file`: `gclone keystore use file`. |

With the sealed store as the default (0.5.1) the rows marked "not measured" are no longer the owner's to try before a command: on a device that was on the plain file, a session of those kinds that runs gclone during the trial and fails stops the move; one that first runs after the move, or on a device that was sealed at its login, fails with the session text and exit 4 until the owner runs `gclone keystore use file` (§15) — after at most ten seconds, also where the framework does not answer at all (rule 5).

**Older binaries on the same machine.** While the device is on `secrets.json` nothing changes for them: gclone 0.4.0 ignores the new files and the backup attribute (measured, and asserted by `tests/keystore.rs` when given a 0.4.0 binary). Once the secrets are sealed — **since 0.5.1 that happens without a command**: at the next login, or at the first run after the trial has passed — gclone 0.4.0 and older say the device is not connected (exit 4), with nobody having been asked; the automatic move cannot see an older binary on a scheduler's `PATH` (§14 item 4), and its note names the way back. That way is `gclone keystore use file` with the new binary, which restores a byte-identical version-1 `secrets.json` and keeps it. **gclone 0.5.0 reads and writes a sealed store**, whoever made it (the same envelope, the same load and save tables): a downgrade to 0.5.0 works on a sealed device; what it does not do is seal by itself — its `login` on a signed-out device writes the plain file unless `keystore.json` says `enclave`, and it moves nothing. An older `login` on a sealed device writes `secrets.json`; the load table then applies and nothing is lost. **And nothing is moved again** (0.5.1, §17.30): gclone 0.4.0 says "not connected", its owner signs in with it, and a keyed `secrets.json` lies beside the `secrets.sealed` of the earlier move. As first built, 0.5.1 then started a new trial on that plain file and, three days and a restart later, removed it again — the older gclone's job broke a second time, and after the next sign-in a third. A `secrets.sealed` beside a keyed `secrets.json` that is not sealed to the running trial's key now stops the trial and the move (above); both binaries keep working, `status` reads "kept: nothing is tested or moved while secrets.sealed lies beside it" with the warning that names the remedies — update the older gclone and `gclone keystore use enclave`, or `gclone keystore use file` —, and `tests/keystore.rs` shows it with the files alone and with the released 0.4.0 binary. **An older `logout` does not sign a sealed device out** ("nothing to do"; `secrets.sealed` stays, also after its `logout --forget`) — it cannot be fixed from this side, it is printed by `keystore use enclave` and stated in `docs/SECURITY.md`. A long-running older process (`gclone web` of 0.4.0) watches `secrets.json` and stops with its "signed out" message when the move removes it. Nothing on Drive and nothing in `config.json`, `state.db` or `token.json` changes; Linux is not affected (no trial, no sealed store, no move).

**Linux.** The plain 0600 file stays — 0.5.1 changes nothing there: no sealer, so no login seals and nothing is moved — and `gclone keystore use enclave` is refused with the reason. The Secret Service is not used, not even where present: on a headless box there is no session bus, or only a collection that a graphical login unlocks; it does not separate programs of one user; and "works now" says nothing about after the next reboot, which is when unattended jobs must work. A TPM-bound store (`systemd-creds`) would plug in as a `Sealer`; not designed.

### 8.3 Locking
`<state>/lock` with `std::fs::File::lock()` (exclusive, kernel-released on process death). Mutating commands (`login` once the vault id is known, `logout`, `passwd`, `copy`, `sync`, `mkdir`, `rm`, `mv`, `restore`, `gc`, `repair`) block-wait up to 5 s then fail with "another gclone is running on this vault" (the CLI adds that nothing was changed, to run the command again when the other one is done, and how to find it, §17.14); read-only commands `try_lock` and fall back to an unrefreshed replica.

A process **without** the lock writes nothing to the state when it opens it (§17.11): `open_ctx` uses `Db::open_shared` (no file creation, no schema creation or upgrade; `StateError::Locked` if the database has no schema yet — the lock holder is creating it, and two processes that both saw an empty database would both try) and `Vault::open_unlocked` (plain reads of `vault_id`, `device_id` and the pending high-water mark; no device-name write, no machine-fingerprint check, no rotation, no index-cache directory). SQLite's WAL lets such a reader proceed while the lock holder is inside a write transaction of any length (`rebuild_from` loads a whole snapshot in one), whereas the `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` that `Vault::open` uses waits `busy_timeout` (5 s) and then fails with "database is locked" — which is what a read-only command did before, instead of printing "note: index not refreshed (another gclone is running)". The lock holder's `Vault::open` writes `device_name` only when it changed. Not covered: what a lock-less command writes later (the download ledger of `cat` / `check --download`, the `trashed_ms` mark that `check` clears) is a single statement each and still waits for a writer.

`gclone web` (§7.4) is a long-lived process and holds the lock **only** while it starts and while a refresh runs: in between it is a lock-less reader in the sense above (`open_shared` / `open_unlocked` for its whole life), and each refresh opens a locked vault of its own on a fresh connection (`state::try_lock_existing` — which, unlike `try_lock`, creates neither the directory nor the lock file: a viewer must not bring back state that `logout --forget` removed — then `cli::context::open_replica`) and drops it. Its ledger writes go through a separate connection so that one that waits for another process's write transaction holds up no query.
`gclone serve restic` (§7.6) takes **no lock** and opens no state: it cannot hold up `sync`, `web` or another `serve restic`, and none of them holds it up. Several of them refresh the access token on their own (single-flight inside a process; Google's refresh tokens do not rotate; `token.json` is replaced atomically): two refreshing at once make one request too many.

**The secrets lock** (0.5.0, §8.2): `<state root>/secrets.lock`, a kernel lock (`File::lock`, released when the process dies), created 0600 by the first writer.
- **Writers** — `login` around each save and around the move at its end, `logout`, the move of `gclone keystore use`, the automatic move (0.5.1) — hold it exclusively. `login` never holds it across the sign-in or a passphrase prompt; `keystore use` takes it after its questions. They wait up to 5 s (`keystore::WRITER_WAIT`), then fail with `ConfigError::KeyStoreBusy`: "another gclone is changing this device's sign-in … Nothing was changed" — **except the automatic move, which tries once and does nothing when the lock is busy**: no command waits for a step it did not ask for. Under the lock a writer may open the sealed store (a save into it, `keystore use file`, the moves, `settle_sealed`); each such call into the enclave is bounded at ten seconds (§8.2 rule 5), so a session in which the framework does not answer gives the lock back with an error instead of keeping it for the life of a process (0.5.1, §17.30: a hung `keystore use file` used to keep a working session from the remedy).
- **Readers take no lock on the normal path.** Each file is replaced by rename, so a reader sees one whole version of it, and `secrets.sealed` is self-contained. A move creates the new file before it removes the old one: towards `secrets.sealed`, a reader that misses `secrets.json` finds the sealed file; towards `secrets.json`, a reader that looked for `secrets.json` too early and for `secrets.sealed` too late looks at `secrets.json` a **third** time and finds it (measured, §17.28: two looks found neither file 3 to 21 times per run, three looks never). A third look covers one move; for several moves in a row, a reader that still found nothing looks once more under the **shared** lock, where no move is in progress — it waits at most 2 s, only in this case, and then looks one last time. A reader never creates the lock file.
- **The trial's record** is written without the lock (§8.2).
- **Watchers.** `gclone web`'s `DeviceGuard` and the sign-out watcher of `serve restic --port` ask `Paths::secrets_presence()`: the stamp of `secrets.json`, else of `secrets.sealed`, else of `secrets.json` again; if all three are absent, the shared lock is tried without waiting — busy → "present, look again at the next tick"; free → both files are looked at under it. `DeviceGuard`'s reload after a stamp changed treats a load **error** as "look again at the next tick": only `Ok(None)` or another login digest means signed out. So a move under a running viewer or listener — the automatic one included — is no sign-out, and `gclone logout` of a sealed device ends them as it does for the plain file.

### 8.4 SQLite schema (`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=FULL; PRAGMA user_version=1`)
```sql
CREATE TABLE meta(k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v BLOB NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;
  -- keys: device_id(8 bytes), device_name, next_seq(u64 BE), lamport(u64 BE), machine_fp(32 bytes),
  --       base_snapshot_name, base_snapshot_lamport, base_snapshot_size, snap_checked, last_snapshot_name, last_snapshot_id, last_snapshot_size,
  --       last_snapshot_created_ms, data_folder_id, data_folder_n, data_folder_count, vault_format, vault_name, last_refresh_ms,
  --       vault_id (16 bytes; Vault::open refuses a state.db of another vault with StateError::Corrupt), base_snapshot_id, last_snapshot_md5   (§17.3; no schema change)
  --       base_snapshot_md5 (16 bytes; presence rule (b), §5.3), cleanup_done (32 bytes; §5.6), remembered (postcard: name, file id, created_ms? of
  --       segments known before a rebuild and not applied again yet; §5.3), resolve_all (present = the next resolution scans every head; §5.2.3)   (§17.11)
CREATE TABLE heads(path TEXT NOT NULL, st_l INTEGER NOT NULL, st_d BLOB NOT NULL, st_i INTEGER NOT NULL,
  kind INTEGER NOT NULL, size INTEGER NOT NULL, mtime_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, exec INTEGER NOT NULL, hash BLOB NOT NULL,
  blob BLOB, off INTEGER, clen INTEGER, salt BLOB, chunk_log2 INTEGER, epoch INTEGER, suite INTEGER, flags INTEGER,   -- Loc or NULLs
  o_l INTEGER, o_d BLOB, o_i INTEGER,                       -- origin stamp or NULLs
  winner INTEGER NOT NULL,                                  -- 1 for the max-stamp head of the path
  PRIMARY KEY(path, st_l, st_d, st_i, hash)) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX heads_size ON heads(size) WHERE winner = 1;
CREATE INDEX heads_blob ON heads(blob);
CREATE INDEX heads_losers ON heads(path) WHERE winner = 0;                   -- the conflict losers: conflict count and resolution rule 1 in O(losers) (§5.2.3)
CREATE TABLE touched(path TEXT PRIMARY KEY) WITHOUT ROWID;                    -- paths whose heads changed since the last complete resolution (rule 2, §5.2.3)
CREATE TABLE removed( /* same columns as heads without winner */ …, removed_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,
  by_l INTEGER NOT NULL, by_d BLOB NOT NULL, by_i INTEGER NOT NULL,          -- stamp of the superseding op (smallest one, §5.2.2)
  PRIMARY KEY(path, st_l, st_d, st_i, hash)) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE INDEX removed_blob ON removed(blob);
CREATE TABLE blobs(id BLOB PRIMARY KEY, file_id TEXT NOT NULL, clen INTEGER NOT NULL, md5 BLOB NOT NULL,
  created_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, trashed_ms INTEGER) WITHOUT ROWID;            -- trashed_ms: set by gc on this device; such rows survive rebuilds (§5.3, §5.9)
CREATE TABLE devices(id BLOB PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, first_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, last_ms INTEGER NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE applied(dev BLOB NOT NULL, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, hash BLOB NOT NULL, file_id TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL,
  lamport INTEGER NOT NULL, created_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, size INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(dev, seq, hash)) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE base_covers(dev BLOB PRIMARY KEY, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, hash BLOB NOT NULL, file_id TEXT NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;   -- tips of the base snapshot
CREATE TABLE base_covered(dev BLOB NOT NULL, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, h4 BLOB NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(dev, seq, h4)) WITHOUT ROWID;   -- its exact coverage set
CREATE TABLE hw(dev BLOB PRIMARY KEY, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, hash BLOB NOT NULL, file_id TEXT NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;   -- rollback marks (§5.3)
CREATE TABLE own(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, hash BLOB NOT NULL, file_id TEXT NOT NULL);   -- segments sealed under the current device id
CREATE TABLE blocked(name TEXT PRIMARY KEY, first_seen_ms INTEGER NOT NULL) WITHOUT ROWID;   -- local clock
CREATE TABLE pending(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, draft BLOB NOT NULL, created_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, pid INTEGER NOT NULL);
  -- draft = postcard(OpDraft) (§9.3)
CREATE TABLE outbox(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, file_id TEXT NOT NULL, bytes BLOB NOT NULL, effects BLOB NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE pairs(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, local_root TEXT NOT NULL, remote_prefix TEXT NOT NULL,
  root_ino INTEGER NOT NULL, root_birth_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, fold_case INTEGER NOT NULL, UNIQUE(local_root, remote_prefix));
CREATE TABLE base(pair INTEGER NOT NULL, key TEXT NOT NULL, rel TEXT NOT NULL, kind INTEGER NOT NULL,
  size INTEGER NOT NULL, mtime_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, ctime_ns INTEGER NOT NULL, ino INTEGER NOT NULL, mode INTEGER NOT NULL,
  hash BLOB NOT NULL, st_l INTEGER NOT NULL, st_d BLOB NOT NULL, st_i INTEGER NOT NULL, observed_ns INTEGER NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY(pair, key)) WITHOUT ROWID;
CREATE TABLE ledger(ts_ms INTEGER NOT NULL, dir INTEGER NOT NULL /* 0 = uploaded, 1 = downloaded */, bytes INTEGER NOT NULL);
```
Integer binding: rusqlite implements `ToSql`/`FromSql` for `u64` only behind its `fallible_uint` feature (enabled in §9.1); those conversions fail above `i64::MAX`. Therefore inode numbers (`base.ino`, `pairs.root_ino`) — which some network and FUSE file systems set above 2^63 — are stored **bit-cast** (`as i64` when binding, `as u64` when reading), never converted. All other `u64` values (sequence numbers, lamports, sizes, offsets, millisecond timestamps) are below 2^63 by construction and go through the fallible conversions; a failure there is `StateError::Corrupt`.

`heads_losers` and `touched` were added after the first builds (§17.11) and are part of schema version 1: `Db::open` creates them in a version-1 database that lacks them (`CREATE … IF NOT EXISTS` in one transaction that also sets `resolve_all`: nothing tracked the paths touched so far). `Db::open_shared` (§8.3) never does — only the lock holder changes the schema.

`state.db` is rebuildable from Drive except `pending`/`outbox` (unpublished work), `hw` (rollback marks), `own`, the `trashed_ms` marks and `base` (losing it only makes the next sync conservative: nothing is deleted or overwritten).

---

## 9. Rust architecture

One crate `gclone` (library + binary), edition 2024, MSRV 1.89, Unix only (macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux). The engine is generic over `B: Backend`; the binary uses `AnyBackend`.

### 9.1 `Cargo.toml`
```toml
[package]
name = "gclone"
version = "0.2.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.89"

[lib]
name = "gclone"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "gclone"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
# --- compile-verified set from RESEARCH.md §4 ---
tokio = { version = "1.54", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "fs", "io-util", "io-std", "net", "sync", "time", "signal"] }   # io-std: tokio::io::stdout() for `cat`
tokio-util = { version = "0.7.20", features = ["io", "rt"] }
futures-util = { version = "0.3.34", default-features = false, features = ["std"] }
bytes = "1.12"
reqwest = { version = "0.13.5", default-features = false, features = ["rustls", "http2", "stream", "json", "query", "form"] }
hyper = { version = "1.12", default-features = false, features = ["http1", "http2", "server"] }   # `gclone web` (§7.4): the HTTP/1 server; in the tree through reqwest, only `server` is new code (§17.20). http2: the stdio transport of `gclone serve restic` (§7.6, §17.24)
hyper-util = { version = "0.1.21", default-features = false, features = ["tokio"] }         # TokioIo / TokioTimer for it
serde = { version = "1.0.229", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0.154"
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "env", "wrap_help"] }
rusqlite = { version = "0.42", features = ["bundled", "fallible_uint"] }   # fallible_uint: ToSql/FromSql for u64 (absent without it in 0.42.0)
indicatif = "0.18.6"
tracing = "0.1.44"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3.23", default-features = false, features = ["fmt", "ansi", "env-filter", "std"] }
ignore = "0.4.34"
anyhow = "1.0.104"
thiserror = "2.0.21"
rpassword = "7.5"
open = "5.4"
filetime = "0.2.29"
blake3 = "1.8.7"
etcetera = "0.11"
url = "2.5.8"
base64 = "0.23"
sha2 = { version = "0.11", features = ["zeroize"] }   # zeroize: SHA-256 states — and the HMAC / HKDF states made of them — are wiped on drop (§17.26)
getrandom = "0.4"
zeroize = "1.9"
# --- compile-verified by WP0 (cargo/rustc 1.99.0, 2026-11-11): every entry resolves and compiles as written; resolved versions: §17.1 ---
chacha20poly1305 = { version = "0.11.0", features = ["zeroize"] }   # zeroize: the cipher object wipes its key copy on drop (§17.2)
poly1305 = { version = "0.9.1", features = ["zeroize"] }            # not used by name: chacha20poly1305's own dependencies, listed for their
cipher = { version = "0.5.2", features = ["zeroize"] }              # `zeroize` features, which chacha20poly1305's does not forward (§17.26)
hkdf = "0.13.0"
argon2 = { version = "0.6.0", default-features = false, features = ["alloc", "zeroize"] }
postcard = { version = "1.1.3", default-features = false, features = ["use-std"] }
md-5 = "0.11.0"                    # 2026 generation (digest 0.11, same trait vocabulary as sha2 0.11); resolves and compiles
caseless = "0.2"                   # Unicode full case folding for path::cmp_key (§5.1)
httpdate = "1"                     # `Date:` header parsing (1.0.3 is already in the dependency tree via hyper)
unicode-normalization = "0.1.24"
libc = "0.2"

[dev-dependencies]
wiremock = "0.6.5"
tempfile = "3.27"
tokio = { version = "1.54", features = ["test-util"] }
hyper = { version = "1.12", default-features = false, features = ["client", "http2"] }   # 0.5.0: the HTTP/2 client of the `serve restic` tests

[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = "fat"
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
strip = "symbols"

[profile.dev.package."*"]
opt-level = 3        # dependencies are optimised in dev/test builds too: the keyfile KDF is Argon2id at 256 MiB (§2.6)

# 0.5.0 (§8.2, §17.28): the Secure Enclave key store. Declarations only; both crates were in the tree already, through
# reqwest's platform certificate verifier, at these versions — Cargo.lock gains no package.
[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
security-framework-sys = "2.17.0"
core-foundation = "0.10.1"
```
Notes: (1) the 2026 RustCrypto generation changed trait names — confine AEAD/HKDF/Argon2 calls to private helper functions in `crypto/stream.rs` / `crypto/kdf.rs` and read docs.rs for 0.11/0.13/0.6. (2) If a pinned feature name does not exist, WP0 fixes `Cargo.toml` and appends an "Errata" section to this spec; nobody else edits `Cargo.toml`. (3) No `proptest`: property tests use the seeded xorshift PRNG in `tests/support/prng.rs`. (4) Not used: `qrcode`, `keyring`, `aes-siv`, any OAuth crate (the device side of §2.4 is two JSON POSTs and a loopback listener), `zstd`, reqwest `gzip`. The v1.2 auth redesign adds no crate: `url` validates the auth URL, `open` launches the browser, `rpassword` reads the passphrase, `unicode-normalization` gives NFC, `sha2` the PKCE challenge. (5) No calendar/time-zone crate: RFC 3339 parsing and civil-date formatting are hand-written in `util.rs`, local time goes through `libc::localtime_r`, HTTP dates through `httpdate` (§9.3). (6) Two rusqlite/tokio features are load-bearing and verified against the local registry sources: `fallible_uint` (rusqlite 0.42.0 gates every `u64` conversion behind it) and `io-std` (tokio gates `stdout()` behind it).

```
tests/restic_http.rs, tests/restic_e2e.rs, tests/support/h2.rs   0.5.0 (§17.24): `serve restic` in process over HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 on the in-memory backend; the binary against FakeDrive, driven by a test client and by the real restic; the HTTP/2 test client both use
.github/scripts/install-restic.sh                              0.5.0: a pinned, checksummed restic for CI

worker/viewer/, worker/scripts/{check-dist,release-bundle,fetch-viewer,check-release,verify-deployed,smoke,stub-dist,headers-file}.mjs, worker/test/{viewer,e2e}/   0.4.0 (§7.5, §16.8): the hosted viewer's browser app and build, the release tooling, its tests
.github/workflows/{ci,release}.yml, .github/scripts/install-wasm-bindgen.sh   §17.17; 0.4.0: the wasm core, the viewer, the browser suite, the attested viewer bundle (§7.5)
worker/test/{seal,login,token,refresh,contract}.test.ts, worker/test/{helpers.ts,tsconfig.json,contract.json}   WP8
```
The Rust crate and `worker/` share no code and no build step. Their contract is §2.3 (HTTP API) and the constants of §2.2 — and, so that the two implementations of that text cannot drift apart unnoticed, **one shared data file**: `worker/test/contract.json` (§16.5), written by WP8 and checked by both the Worker's tests (against the real `handle()`) and WP3's `tests/auth.rs` (against `FakeDrive`'s auth routes and the Rust client).
`mod.rs` files re-export the public items listed below so that the paths used in this spec (`crate::crypto::Sealer`, `crate::index::Vault`, …) resolve.

General API rules: public async trait methods are written `fn f(&self, …) -> impl Future<Output = …> + Send` (shown below as `async fn` for brevity — implementers MUST keep futures `Send`); no `unwrap`/`expect` on I/O, crypto, SQL or network results outside tests; raw key material (`MasterKey`, `PurposeKey`, stream keys, exported key bytes, the passphrase) lives in `Zeroizing`; secrets carried as JSON strings (tokens, base64 keys in `Secrets`/`KeyfilePayload`/`LoginGrant`/`AccessGrant`) are plain `String`s inside types that do **not** implement `Debug`; no module other than `crypto` calls an AEAD, and no module other than `state`/`index` executes SQL. Blocking work (file hashing, sealing, SQLite) runs in `spawn_blocking` or scoped threads with **owned** inputs — never `block_in_place` (it panics on the current-thread runtime that `#[tokio::test]` uses).

### 9.3 WP0 — `types`, `error`, `util`, `path`, `consts`, `ui`
```rust
// ---------- src/types.rs ----------  (all: Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq; serde Serialize/Deserialize where noted S)
// DeviceId and BlobId print as hex: Debug = `DeviceId(a1b2…)`, and both implement Display (the plain hex).
#[derive(Copy, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub struct DeviceId(pub [u8; 8]);            // S
#[derive(Copy, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub struct BlobId(pub [u8; 16]);             // S
#[derive(Copy, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub struct Stamp { pub lamport: u64, pub device: DeviceId, pub idx: u32 }   // S
pub struct Loc { pub blob: BlobId, pub off: u64, pub clen: u64, pub salt: [u8; 16], pub chunk_log2: u8, pub epoch: u32,
                 pub suite: u8, pub flags: u8 }                                      // S  (field order frozen, §4.4)
#[derive(Copy)] pub enum EntryKind { File, Dir }                                     // S
pub struct Entry { pub kind: EntryKind, pub size: u64, pub mtime_ns: i64, pub exec: bool, pub hash: [u8; 32], pub loc: Option<Loc> }  // S
pub struct BlobRec { pub id: BlobId, pub file_id: String, pub clen: u64, pub md5: [u8; 16], pub created_ms: u64 }   // S
pub struct SegRef { pub device: DeviceId, pub seq: u64, pub hash: [u8; 32], pub file_id: String }                  // S
#[derive(Copy, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub struct CoveredSeg { pub device: DeviceId, pub seq: u64, pub h4: [u8; 4] }   // S
#[derive(Copy)] pub struct StatSig { pub size: u64, pub mtime_ns: i64, pub ctime_ns: i64, pub ino: u64, pub mode: u32 }   // S
pub struct Head { pub path: String, pub stamp: Stamp, pub entry: Entry, pub origin: Option<Stamp>, pub winner: bool }
pub struct RemovedVersion { pub path: String, pub stamp: Stamp, pub entry: Entry, pub removed_ms: u64, pub by: Stamp }
pub struct BaseRow { pub key: String, pub rel: String, pub kind: EntryKind, pub sig: StatSig, pub hash: [u8; 32],
                     pub remote_stamp: Stamp, pub observed_ns: i64 }
pub enum BaseEffectKind { Set { sig: StatSig, hash: [u8; 32], observed_ns: i64, kind: EntryKind }, Forget }          // S
pub struct BaseEffect { pub pair: i64, pub key: String, pub rel: String, pub kind: BaseEffectKind }                 // S
pub enum OpDraft {                                                                                                   // S
    VaultInit { format: u16, name: String },
    Device { id: DeviceId, name: String },
    Blob(BlobRec),
    Put { path: String, entry: Entry, base: Option<Stamp>, origin: Option<Stamp>, effect: Option<BaseEffect> },
    Del { path: String, base: Stamp, effect: Option<BaseEffect> },
}
impl DeviceId { pub fn random() -> Self; pub fn hex(&self) -> String; pub fn short(&self) -> String /* 8 hex */; pub fn from_hex(s: &str) -> Option<Self>; }
// from_hex (both ids): exactly 16 / 32 LOWERCASE hex characters — one accepted spelling per id (object names)
impl BlobId   { pub fn random() -> Self; pub fn hex(&self) -> String; pub fn from_hex(s: &str) -> Option<Self>; }
impl Entry    { pub fn dir() -> Self; pub fn empty_file(mtime_ns: i64, exec: bool) -> Self;
                pub fn same_content(&self, o: &Entry) -> bool; }   // equal kind, size, hash — loc, mtime, exec ignored
impl SegRef   { pub fn covered(&self) -> CoveredSeg; }             // (device, seq, hash[0..4])
impl StatSig  { pub fn from_metadata(md: &std::fs::Metadata) -> Self; pub fn is_exec(&self) -> bool; }   // is_exec: the owner-execute bit (mode & 0o100)
impl BaseRow  { pub fn trusted(&self) -> bool; }                 // racy-timestamp rule §5.4

// ---------- src/error.rs ----------  (all: Debug, thiserror::Error)
// Wrapping variants (`#[from]`) are `#[error(transparent)]`: Display shows the innermost message once, and `source()` therefore
// SKIPS the wrapped enum. Never walk `source()` by hand to look inside an error: use `error::find::<T>(&e)` or `exit_code`.
// (Exception: `StateError::Sqlite` keeps a prefix.) QuotaKind and GuardKind implement Display (used in the messages).
pub enum CryptoError { BadMagic, Unsupported(&'static str), WrongKey, Corrupt, Truncated, TrailingData,
                       UnknownEpoch(u32), EpochTooOld { epoch: u32, min: u32 }, Misuse(&'static str), Kdf(String) }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum PathError { Empty, Absolute /* leading '/' */, EmptyComponent /* also a trailing '/' */, DotComponent, Nul, ComponentTooLong, TooLong }
pub enum FormatError { KeyfileDamaged, KeyfileVersion(u32), KdfParams, WeakPassphrase, BadName(String), Codec(u8),
                       BodyVersion(u8) /* the tag of an index object's body enum, §4.6 rule 3 */, Decode(String),
                       IdentityMismatch(String), BadEntry(String) /* §4.6 rules 1 (size), 6–7 */, Path(#[from] PathError), Crypto(#[from] CryptoError) }
impl FormatError { pub fn newer_format(&self) -> Option<String>; }   // Some(what) for the version refusals of §4.6 "Unreadable is not corrupt":
                                                                      // Crypto(Unsupported | UnknownEpoch), Codec, BodyVersion — None for damage
pub enum AuthError { Expired /* /refresh answered invalid_grant: "run gclone login" */, WorkerMisconfigured(String), NotAllowed(String),
                     Denied(String), ScopeMissing, Timeout /* the device code ran out */, LoginFailed(String), BadAuthUrl(String), Network(String),
                     Io(#[from] std::io::Error) }                                    // mapping from Worker answers: §2.4
#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)] pub enum QuotaKind { StorageFull, DailyUpload, DailyDownload, ProjectApiQuota }
pub enum BackendError { NotFound, AlreadyExists, RateLimited, Transient(String), SessionLost, QuotaExceeded(QuotaKind), AppNotAuthorized,
                        Auth(#[from] AuthError), Fatal { status: u16, reason: String, message: String }, Io(#[from] std::io::Error) }
impl BackendError { pub fn is_temporary(&self) -> bool; }        // QuotaExceeded(_) | RateLimited | Transient(_)
pub enum StateError { Sqlite(#[from] rusqlite::Error), Locked, Corrupt(String), Io(#[from] std::io::Error) }
pub enum IndexError { Gap { names: Vec<String> }, Rollback { device: DeviceId, seq: u64 }, VaultTrashed, VaultMissing, VaultNotVisible,
                      NeedsNewerGclone, UnsupportedObject { name: String, what: String } /* an index object in a newer format, §4.6 */,
                      OutboxStuck(String) /* a sealed segment could not be published yet; the text names the cause */,
                      Format(#[from] FormatError), Crypto(#[from] CryptoError),
                      Backend(#[from] BackendError), State(#[from] StateError), Io(#[from] std::io::Error) }
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)] pub enum GuardKind { EmptySource, RevertedTree { suspicious: usize }, DeleteLimit { deletes: u64, total: u64 }, MaxDelete { deletes: u64, limit: u64 } /* an explicit --max-delete: never confirmable, §5.5.2 */, RootChanged }
pub enum TransferError { SourceChanged(String), SourceUnreadable { path: String, err: std::io::Error }, BlobMissing(String),
                         Verify(String), UnsafeTarget(String), TargetCollision(String) /* §5.7 step 3: folded spelling in the way */,
                         Cancelled, Backend(#[from] BackendError),
                         Crypto(#[from] CryptoError), Format(#[from] FormatError),
                         Index(#[from] IndexError), State(#[from] StateError), Io(#[from] std::io::Error) }
pub enum SyncError { Guard(GuardKind), Partial { failed: usize, skipped: usize }, Interrupted, Usage(String),
                     Index(#[from] IndexError), Transfer(#[from] TransferError), Backend(#[from] BackendError),
                     State(#[from] StateError), Io(#[from] std::io::Error) }
pub enum ConfigError { NotConfigured /* no config.json */,
                       NotLoggedIn /* config.json but no secrets file (either backend), or a Drive vault without a refresh token */,
                       Locked /* secrets exist with keys == [] */,
                       InsecurePermissions(String) /* secrets file or its directory: foreign owner or group/other bits (§8.1); the path */,
                       WrongPassphrase, Version(u32), Json(String), Auth(#[from] AuthError) /* a stored auth_url that no longer validates */,
                       Crypto(#[from] CryptoError), Io(#[from] std::io::Error) }
/// Walks the whole chain — every link of the anyhow chain, typed values attached with `.context(err)`, and everything nested
/// in a wrapping variant; mapping and precedence of §7.2:
/// 3 ← CryptoError, FormatError::{KeyfileDamaged, KeyfileVersion},
///     IndexError::{Gap, Rollback, VaultTrashed, VaultMissing, NeedsNewerGclone, UnsupportedObject}, TransferError::Verify
///     (a wrong passphrase never reaches this function as CryptoError::WrongKey: the login flow turns the keyfile's WrongKey into
///      ConfigError::WrongPassphrase first, §2.6)
/// 4 ← AuthError, ConfigError::{NotConfigured, NotLoggedIn, Locked, InsecurePermissions, WrongPassphrase}, IndexError::VaultNotVisible,
///     BackendError::AppNotAuthorized
/// 75 ← QuotaExceeded(_), RateLimited, IndexError::OutboxStuck
/// 5 ← SyncError::Guard      6 ← SyncError::Partial      130 ← Interrupted / Cancelled      2 ← SyncError::Usage      1 ← everything else
pub fn exit_code(e: &anyhow::Error) -> i32;
/// The first error of type T anywhere inside `e` (anyhow chain, context values, wrapping variants): e.g. the AuthError inside
/// SyncError::Index(IndexError::Backend(BackendError::Auth(..))). The CLI uses it to pick the §2.8 text.
pub fn find<T: std::error::Error + 'static>(e: &anyhow::Error) -> Option<&T>;

                 Skip { path: String, reason: String },
                 Warn { message: String },
                 Summary { uploaded: u64, downloaded: u64, reused: u64, deleted: u64, skipped: u64, failed: u64, conflicts: u64,
                           bytes_up: u64, bytes_down: u64, exit: i32 } }

#[derive(Clone)] pub struct Progress { /* cloneable handle; Send + Sync + 'static */ }
impl Ui {
    pub fn new(opts: UiOpts) -> Self;          pub fn silent() -> Self;             // silent(): no output, confirm() = false — for tests
    /// "stdout" and "stderr" go into the given sinks; never a TTY, no progress bars — for tests that assert on output.
    #[doc(hidden)] pub fn with_writers(opts: UiOpts, out: Box<dyn std::io::Write + Send>, err: Box<dyn std::io::Write + Send>) -> Self;
    pub fn quiet(&self) -> bool;               pub fn verbose(&self) -> u8;
    pub fn is_tty(&self) -> bool;              pub fn json(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn out(&self, line: &str);             // human result line → stdout (suppressed in --json)
    pub fn info(&self, line: &str);            // stderr unless -q
    pub fn warn(&self, line: &str);            pub fn error(&self, line: &str);     // "warning: …" / "error: …" on stderr, also with -q;
                                                                                // under --json warn() emits a `warn` event on stdout instead
    pub fn event(&self, e: &Event);            // --json: NDJSON on stdout; otherwise rendered like the examples of §7.3:
                                               // Plan / Skip → aligned lines on stdout (not with -q); Done → stderr with -v only;
                                               // Warn → warn(); Summary → NOTHING (the command prints its own ▸ line with out())
    pub fn confirm(&self, question: &str) -> bool;                                       // false when not a TTY
    pub fn choose(&self, question: &str, options: &[&str]) -> Option<usize>;             // None when not a TTY (root-identity guard)
    pub fn prompt_line(&self, question: &str) -> std::io::Result<String>;                // question → stderr; one line from stdin (TTY or pipe);
                                                                                         // EOF → UnexpectedEof. All four prompt methods BLOCK:
                                                                                         // call them from spawn_blocking
    pub fn prompt_secret(&self, question: &str) -> std::io::Result<String>;              // rpassword, /dev/tty
    pub fn transfer_progress(&self, label: &str, total_bytes: u64, total_files: u64) -> Progress;
}
impl Progress { pub fn hidden() -> Self;       // draws nothing — for tests and library callers
                pub fn add_bytes(&self, n: u64); pub fn file_done(&self); pub fn blob_done(&self); pub fn finish(&self);
                pub fn bytes(&self) -> u64; pub fn files(&self) -> u64; pub fn blobs(&self) -> u64; }   // totals over all clones (also when hidden)
pub fn init_logging(verbose: u8);              // tracing-subscriber to stderr; honours GCLONE_LOG (an EnvFilter directive string);
                                               // default warn, -v gclone=info, -vv gclone=debug, -vvv trace; safe to call twice
```

### 9.4 WP1 — `crypto`, `format`
```rust
// ---------- src/crypto/keys.rs ----------
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct MasterKey(/* Zeroizing<[u8; 32]> */);            // Clone: keys are moved into spawn_blocking closures; no Debug
impl MasterKey { pub fn generate() -> Self; pub fn from_bytes(b: [u8; 32]) -> Self; pub fn expose(&self) -> &[u8; 32]; }
#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)] pub enum Purpose { Data, Index }
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct PurposeKey(/* Zeroizing<[u8; 32]> */);
impl PurposeKey { pub fn from_raw(b: [u8; 32]) -> Self; }                    // only for K_pass (keyfile, §2.6)
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct Keyring { /* vault_id, BTreeMap<u32, MasterKey>, min_epoch */ }
impl Keyring {
    pub fn new(vault_id: [u8; 16], keys: Vec<(u32, MasterKey)>, min_epoch: u32) -> Result<Self, CryptoError>;   // ≥ 1 key, all ≥ min_epoch
    pub fn vault_id(&self) -> [u8; 16];
    pub fn current_epoch(&self) -> u32;          pub fn min_epoch(&self) -> u32;
    pub fn purpose(&self, epoch: u32, p: Purpose) -> Result<PurposeKey, CryptoError>;      // UnknownEpoch / EpochTooOld
    pub fn export(&self) -> Vec<(u32, zeroize::Zeroizing<[u8; 32]>)>;
    /// Whole container under the current epoch. `ty` must have a purpose key: Bundle → Err(Misuse).
    pub fn seal(&self, ty: StreamType, plaintext: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError>;
    pub fn open(&self, ty: StreamType, container: &[u8]) -> Result<zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, CryptoError>;   // precedence of §4.2
    /// Sealer for one Data stream under the current epoch (suite 1, flags 0, CHUNK_LOG2, fresh salt).
    pub fn data_sealer(&self) -> Sealer;
    /// Opener for a Data stream described by an index entry. Order: loc.suite != 1 or loc.flags != 0 → Unsupported (no key is
    /// derived); chunk_log2 outside 12..=24 → Unsupported; then UnknownEpoch / EpochTooOld; then the stream key from the Loc.
    pub fn data_opener(&self, loc: &Loc) -> Result<Opener, CryptoError>;
}

// ---------- src/crypto/stream.rs ----------
pub const HEADER_LEN: usize = 60;   pub const TAG_LEN: usize = 16;   pub const MAGIC: [u8; 4] = *b"GCS1";   pub const SUITE_V1: u8 = 1;
#[repr(u8)] #[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum StreamType { Data = 1, Segment = 2, Snapshot = 3, Bundle = 5 }     // 4 is reserved (blob manifest) and rejected as Unsupported
impl StreamType { pub fn from_u8(b: u8) -> Option<Self>; pub fn purpose(self) -> Option<Purpose>; /* Bundle → None */ }
pub struct Header { pub suite: u8, pub chunk_log2: u8, pub ty: StreamType, pub flags: u8, pub epoch: u32,
                    pub salt: [u8; 16], pub commit: [u8; 32] }
impl Header { pub fn encode(&self) -> [u8; HEADER_LEN];
              /// Steps 1–2 of the §4.2 precedence: Truncated, BadMagic, then Unsupported for suite, chunk_log2 range, type, flags (in that order).
              pub fn decode(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Header, CryptoError>; }
pub fn chunk_count(plain_len: u64, chunk_log2: u8) -> u64;
pub fn ciphertext_len(plain_len: u64, chunk_log2: u8) -> u64;
pub fn plaintext_len(cipher_len: u64, chunk_log2: u8) -> Option<u64>;        // exact definition in §4.2
pub struct ChunkSpan { pub first: u64, pub last: u64 /* inclusive */, pub cipher: std::ops::Range<u64> /* relative to container start */,
                       pub skip: usize /* plaintext bytes to drop from chunk `first` */ }
pub fn chunk_range(plain: std::ops::Range<u64>, plain_len: u64, chunk_log2: u8) -> Option<ChunkSpan>;   // None if empty/out of bounds
pub fn chunk_cipher_len(idx: u64, plain_len: u64, chunk_log2: u8) -> usize;                             // ct+tag length of chunk idx
pub struct Sealer { /* stream key, header, next index, finished */ }
impl Sealer {
    pub fn new(key: &PurposeKey, ty: StreamType, epoch: u32, chunk_log2: u8) -> Sealer;     // fresh random salt; NO salt/nonce parameter
    pub fn header(&self) -> [u8; HEADER_LEN];        pub fn salt(&self) -> [u8; 16];
    /// Appends ct‖tag to `out`. Errors (Misuse): called after the final chunk; pt.len() > C; pt.len() < C and !last;
    /// empty pt unless it is the first and final chunk.
    pub fn seal_chunk(&mut self, pt: &[u8], last: bool, out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), CryptoError>;
    pub fn is_finished(&self) -> bool;
}
pub struct Opener { /* stream key, header bytes, chunk_log2 */ }
impl Opener {
    /// For self-describing streams (index objects, keyfile): Header::decode, then type != expect → WrongKey, then commit → WrongKey.
    pub fn from_header(key: &PurposeKey, header: &[u8], expect: StreamType) -> Result<Opener, CryptoError>;
    /// For Data streams: everything comes from the index entry; the stored header is never trusted. Callers normally use
    /// Keyring::data_opener, which performs the suite/flags/epoch checks first.
    pub fn for_data(key: &PurposeKey, loc: &Loc) -> Result<Opener, CryptoError>;
    pub fn expected_header(&self) -> [u8; HEADER_LEN];
    pub fn chunk_log2(&self) -> u8;
    /// `ct` = exactly one chunk's ct‖tag; appends plaintext to `out` only after the tag verified. Corrupt on failure.
    pub fn open_chunk(&self, idx: u64, last: bool, ct: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), CryptoError>;
}
pub fn seal_all(key: &PurposeKey, ty: StreamType, epoch: u32, chunk_log2: u8, pt: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>;
pub fn open_all(key: &PurposeKey, ty: StreamType, container: &[u8]) -> Result<zeroize::Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>, CryptoError>;  // Truncated/TrailingData/Corrupt/WrongKey
// #[cfg(test)] only: Sealer::with_salt_for_tests(key, ty, epoch, chunk_log2, salt). Reachable only from unit tests in this file —
// that is where the fixed-salt KATs of §4.7 live.

// ---------- src/crypto/kdf.rs ----------   (passphrase → K_pass for the keyfile, §2.6; nothing else uses Argon2)
pub const PREAMBLE_LEN: usize = 36;
#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)] pub struct KdfParams { pub m_kib: u32, pub t: u32, pub p: u32 }
impl Default for KdfParams { /* 262144, 3, 1 — what production code writes */ }
impl KdfParams { pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), FormatError>; }        // accepted bounds of §2.6: m_kib 8192..=524288, t 1..=4, p == 1
pub struct KdfPreamble { pub params: KdfParams, pub salt: [u8; 16] }
impl KdfPreamble { pub fn generate(params: KdfParams) -> Self;               // fresh random salt
                   pub fn encode(&self) -> [u8; PREAMBLE_LEN]; pub fn decode(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, FormatError>; }   // decode validates the bounds
pub struct Passphrase { /* text: Zeroizing<String> — the normalised text; legacy: Option<Zeroizing<String>>; no Debug, no Display */ }
impl Passphrase {
    pub fn from_input(input: &str) -> Self;                                   // normalisation of §2.6 for ENTERING a passphrase
    pub fn for_setting(input: &str) -> Self;                                  // what a keyfile is sealed under: the text gclone 0.4.0 makes of the input (§2.6, §17.29)
    pub fn set_checked(input: &str) -> Result<Self, FormatError>;             // for_setting + PASSPHRASE_MIN_CHARS → WeakPassphrase
    pub fn readings(&self) -> Vec<Passphrase>;                                // the canonical reading, then the text as typed where that is another one
    pub fn looks_generated(&self) -> bool;                                    // the 26-symbol shape, not in the canonical form: a typed passphrase, exact in spelling
    pub fn generate() -> Self;                                                // 26 Crockford symbols, 130 bits (0.5.0; 20 and 100 before)
    pub fn legacy(&self) -> Option<Passphrase>;                               // the same input as gclone before 0.5.0 normalised it, if that
                                                                              // differs (a 26-symbol shape not typed canonically, §2.6)
    pub fn display(&self) -> zeroize::Zeroizing<String>;                      // the text to show once after generate()
    pub fn char_count(&self) -> usize;                                        // Unicode scalar values (for the warning below PASSPHRASE_WARN_CHARS)
}
/// K_pass (§2.6). Blocking (≈ 1 s, 256 MiB with the default parameters): call it from spawn_blocking.
pub fn derive_pass_key(pass: &Passphrase, pre: &KdfPreamble) -> Result<PurposeKey, CryptoError>;

// ---------- src/format/index.rs ----------   (types of §4.6 with serde derives: SegmentV1, SnapshotV1, Op, HeadRec, RemovedRec, DeviceRec)
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum IndexName { Segment { device: DeviceId, seq: u64, h8: [u8; 4] }, Snapshot { lamport: u64, device: DeviceId, h8: [u8; 4] } }

pub fn segment_name(device: DeviceId, seq: u64, hash: &[u8; 32]) -> String;
pub fn snapshot_name(lamport: u64, device: DeviceId, hash: &[u8; 32]) -> String;
pub struct SealedObject { pub name: String, pub hash: [u8; 32], pub bytes: Vec<u8> }
pub fn seal_segment(keys: &Keyring, seg: &SegmentV1) -> Result<SealedObject, FormatError>;     // validates paths and entries first (§4.6 rules 5–6); > INDEX_OBJECT_MAX → BadEntry (seal_snapshot too)
pub fn seal_snapshot(keys: &Keyring, snap: &SnapshotV1) -> Result<SealedObject, FormatError>;  // rules 5–7
pub fn open_segment(keys: &Keyring, name: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(SegmentV1, [u8; 32]), FormatError>;   // acceptance rules §4.6; FormatError::newer_format tells "newer" from "damaged"
pub fn open_snapshot(keys: &Keyring, name: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(SnapshotV1, [u8; 32]), FormatError>;
pub fn op_from_draft(d: &OpDraft) -> Op;                                                         // drops the BaseEffect

// ---------- src/format/blob.rs ----------   (v1 blobs have no trailer, §4.5)

pub fn data_folder_name(device: DeviceId, n: u32) -> String;

// ---------- src/format/keyfile.rs ----------   (§2.6; KeyfileKey and KeyfilePayload hold secrets: NO Debug derive)
pub const KEYFILE_PREFIX: &str = "gclone-key-";
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct KeyfileKey { pub epoch: u32, pub key: String }
// `gen` is a reserved keyword in edition 2024: the Rust identifier is `generation` everywhere; only the JSON key and the object name
// keep the wire spelling "gen".
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct KeyfilePayload { pub v: u32, pub vault_id: String, #[serde(rename = "gen")] pub generation: u32, pub keys: Vec<KeyfileKey>,
                            pub min_epoch: u32, pub created_ms: u64, pub by: String }
impl KeyfilePayload { pub fn from_keyring(keys: &Keyring, generation: u32, by: &str, now_ms: u64) -> Self;
                      pub fn keyring(&self) -> Result<Keyring, FormatError>;       // uses self.vault_id
                      pub fn vault_id_bytes(&self) -> Result<[u8; 16], FormatError>; }

pub fn parse_keyfile_name(name: &str) -> Option<(u32 /* generation */, [u8; 4] /* h8 */)>;
/// KdfPreamble::generate(params) → derive_pass_key → Stream(type Bundle, epoch 0) over the JSON payload. Blocking (Argon2id).
/// `params` is KdfParams::default() everywhere outside tests.
pub fn seal_keyfile(p: &KeyfilePayload, pass: &Passphrase, params: KdfParams) -> Result<SealedObject, FormatError>;
/// What open_keyfile checks before it derives a key (§2.6): name, size, the name's h8, the KDF preamble's bounds. Passing = a
/// well-formed keyfile: it can be tried, at the cost the preamble names. ATTACH and the hosted viewer pick candidates with it.
pub fn check_keyfile(name: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(u32 /* generation */, KdfPreamble), FormatError>;
/// Open order and errors of §2.6 (size, name, h8, KDF bounds — before any Argon2 allocation —, Argon2id, commit → Crypto(WrongKey),
/// chunks, JSON, generation/keys). Blocking. After WrongKey, `pass.legacy()` — if there is one — is tried the same way.
pub fn open_keyfile(name: &str, bytes: &[u8], pass: &Passphrase) -> Result<KeyfilePayload, FormatError>;

impl VaultDescriptor { pub fn new(vault_id: [u8; 16]) -> Self; pub fn to_bytes(&self) -> Vec<u8>; pub fn parse(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, FormatError>; }
```
