### 16.2 Configuration
| Binding | Kind | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` | secret (`wrangler secret put`) | the ID of the client of type "TVs and Limited Input devices": every login, and the refresh tokens those logins issue |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | secret | its secret — exists nowhere else |
| `GOOGLE_LEGACY_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_LEGACY_CLIENT_SECRET` | secrets, **optional**, used only when both are set | **0.4.0**: the "Web application" client — the hosted viewer's sign-in (`/web/*`, §2.3) and nothing else; its only Authorized redirect URI is `https://<host>/callback`. (0.2.0–0.3.x: used by `/refresh` for requests without `"client": "device"`; that branch is closed, §17.22. The names were kept so that an existing deployment needs no change.) |
| `SEAL_KEY` | secret, **optional** (0.4.0) | 32 random bytes in base64 or base64url: the key that seals the viewer's session cookie (§2.3). Anything else counts as not set. A freshly generated value at the 0.4.0 deployment — never one from before 0.2.0; a new value ends every browser session and no device login. With the pair above it switches the viewer's sign-in on. |
| `ALLOWED_EMAILS` | secret — **only** a secret, never a `vars` entry | comma-separated Google account addresses; empty or not set = nobody. Compared byte for byte but for the case of ASCII letters; an entry that is not printable ASCII matches nobody (§2.3) |
| `RATE_LIMIT` | rate-limit binding (`ratelimits` in `wrangler.jsonc`; no storage product, no namespace to create) | `AUTH_RATE_LIMIT`: 30 requests / 60 s per key — the client's IPv4 address or IPv6 /64 (§2.3) |
| `ASSETS` | static-assets binding (`assets` in `wrangler.jsonc`; 0.4.0) | the viewer's files in `./dist`: read-only, uploaded with the Worker, changed only by a deploy. The Worker reads `index.html` from it and nothing else; `/a/*` and `/sw.js` are served by the asset layer without running the Worker (§16.8) |

No KV, D1, R2, Durable Object, queue, cron or service binding; the assets binding is not storage. A custom domain — recommended (§16.6), and required for the hosted viewer — is a `routes` entry in this file with `"workers_dev": false` (the device client names no URL; the web client names `https://<host>/callback`). The file as specified, shown for the `workers.dev` host:
```jsonc
// worker/wrangler.jsonc
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/wrangler/config-schema.json",
  "name": "gclone-auth",
  "main": "src/entry.ts",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-11-01",
  "workers_dev": true,
  "preview_urls": false,
  "observability": {
    "enabled": true,
    "redact_query_string": true,
    "logs": { "invocation_logs": false },
    "traces": { "enabled": false }
  },
  "ratelimits": [ { "name": "RATE_LIMIT", "namespace_id": "1001", "simple": { "limit": 30, "period": 60 } } ],
  "assets": { "directory": "./dist", "binding": "ASSETS", "run_worker_first": ["/*", "!/a/*", "!/sw.js"],
              "html_handling": "none", "not_found_handling": "none" }
}
```
These things in this file are **security requirements**, asserted by `scripts/check-config.mjs` on every `npm test`:
- **The file holds the allowed keys and nothing else** (§17.19). Top level: `$schema`, `name`, `main`, `compatibility_date`, `compatibility_flags`, `workers_dev`, `preview_urls`, `routes`, `observability`, `ratelimits`, and since 0.4.0 `assets`. Under `observability`: `enabled`, `head_sampling_rate`, `redact_query_string`, `logs` (`enabled`, `head_sampling_rate`, `invocation_logs`), `traces` (`enabled`). In a `routes` entry: `pattern`, `custom_domain`, `zone_id`, `zone_name`. In the `ratelimits` entry: `name`, `namespace_id`, `simple` (`limit`, `period`). Every other key is a problem, whatever its name — a list of forbidden names cannot know every binding type Cloudflare has or will have. Two consequences are spelled out in the messages: **no `unsafe`** (`unsafe.bindings` attaches a binding of any type, a KV namespace included) and **no `env`** (a wrangler environment inherits no bindings, so `wrangler deploy --env <name>` would deploy a Worker without the rate limiter — and the Worker lets every request through when `env.RATE_LIMIT` is undefined, §16.3; the limiter is also what keeps one sender from mass-producing device codes, §2.3.2).
- **Plain line feeds** (§17.23). The check reads JSON plus whole-line `//` comments, a line ending at a line feed; wrangler's reader ends a `//` comment at a lone carriage return and at U+2028 / U+2029 as well. `// note<CR>"kv_namespaces": […]` would therefore be one comment line to the check and a binding to wrangler (measured with `wrangler deploy --dry-run`), and one line in most diff views. A file with a carriage return that no line feed follows, or with one of the two separators — anywhere, a string included — is refused before anything is parsed, with the line and the code point. CR LF is fine: the same lines for both readers.
- **`main` is `src/entry.ts`, and the `assets` entry is exactly the object above** (0.4.0), key by key and value by value: the Worker runs first for every path except `/a/*` and `/sw.js` and alone decides what a path means (no file of `./dist` is reachable under its own name, no HTML path rewriting, no single-page fallback); the two exceptions cost no Worker request and meet no rate limit. `run_worker_first: true` would be as safe and is refused only for that reason; any other value would hand files out without the Worker.
- **Nothing of a request is stored beyond the Worker's own log line** — four settings, all required. From 0.2.0 to 0.3.x no route carried a secret in its URL (device codes and tokens travel in POST bodies) and these were a second line; since 0.4.0 Google's redirect to `/callback` carries the authorization code of a browser sign-in in its query (single-use, useless without the verifier in the tab), and they are what keeps it out of what Cloudflare stores:
  - **`logs.invocation_logs: false`.** With observability on, Cloudflare by default stores one invocation log per request with the method, the full URL and headers, kept for days and readable by anyone with log access to the account, whatever the code passes to `console.log`.
  - **`redact_query_string: true`.** Switching invocation logs off removes only that separate event. Cloudflare attaches the triggering request to **every** stored log event — the Worker's own one-line logs included — and to traces (the telemetry event type carries `$metadata.url`, "Request URL that triggered the Worker invocation", and `$workers.event` on events of type `cf-worker-log`; [K], read from Cloudflare's API types, not observed on an account). This key ("Whether query strings are removed from request URLs in logs and traces", default `false`; present in wrangler 4.160.1, the floor in `package.json`) removes the query string there.
  - **`traces: { enabled: false }`.** Traces record requests as well; nothing here needs them, and the top-level `enabled: true` must not start them when Cloudflare changes that default.
  - **No `destinations`** (under `logs` or `traces`), **no `tail_consumers` / `streaming_tail_consumers`, no `logpush`**: nothing exports logs or traces out of the account.
- **`preview_urls: false`.** Preview URLs serve each uploaded version of the Worker under its own `<version>-gclone-auth.<acct>.workers.dev` host: an old version — one from before a security fix, with the current secrets — would stay reachable, and outside any zone rule of a custom domain. (With the key omitted Cloudflare derives the setting from `workers_dev`; pinning it makes the shipped state independent of that.)
- **No `vars`.** Vars and secrets share one binding namespace: while the deployed version has a var `ALLOWED_EMAILS`, `wrangler secret put ALLOWED_EMAILS` is refused, and every `wrangler deploy` from a file with `"vars": { "ALLOWED_EMAILS": "" }` would re-assert the empty value — an empty allowlist, every login refused ([K]: Wrangler behaviour from memory, not re-checked). The allowlist is therefore a secret only, the shipped file has no `vars` key, and the code treats an undefined `env.ALLOWED_EMAILS` as empty.
- **The `ratelimits` entry** — exactly one, named `RATE_LIMIT`, `simple: { limit: 30, period: 60 }`, and with `ASSETS` the Worker's only binding (Workers Rate Limiting binding; [K]: key name and shape as of wrangler 4.36 — if the installed wrangler rejects it, WP8 corrects the key and records it in the Errata). `namespace_id` is any integer string unique within the account; `period` must be 10 or 60.

`secrets.required` is deliberately **not** declared: `wrangler deploy` fails while a required secret is missing, and the first deploy has to happen before the Google app's branding can name the Worker's host. The Worker checks its configuration at request time instead (`server_misconfigured`, §2.3). No `compatibility_flags`: no Node API is used.

### 16.3 Code structure (signatures are the contract between the source files and the tests; the 0.4.0 additions are in §16.8)
```ts
// ---------- src/index.ts ----------
export interface RateLimiter { limit(options: { key: string }): Promise<{ success: boolean }> }      // the shape of a Workers rate-limit binding
export interface AssetFetcher { fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response> }                         // 0.4.0: the shape of the static-assets binding
export interface Env { GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: string; GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: string;            // the device client
                       GOOGLE_LEGACY_CLIENT_ID?: string; GOOGLE_LEGACY_CLIENT_SECRET?: string;   // optional, used when both are set: the web client, /web/* only (0.4.0)
                       SEAL_KEY?: string;              // 0.4.0, optional: 32 bytes in base64, the key of the viewer's session cookie
                       ALLOWED_EMAILS?: string;        // a secret; undefined (not yet put) = empty = nobody
                       RATE_LIMIT?: RateLimiter;       // absent in unit tests: then nothing is limited
                       ASSETS?: AssetFetcher }         // 0.4.0: the viewer's files; absent: `/` and `/callback` are the Worker's own home page
export interface Deps {
  fetch: (input: string | URL | Request, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;   // every request to Google goes through this — tests inject a fake
  now: () => number;                                                                 // 0.4.0: milliseconds — when a web session starts and when it has run out
  google: { deviceCodeUrl: string; tokenUrl: string; revokeUrl: string; authUrl: string };   // §2.2 constants by default (authUrl: 0.4.0)
}
export const GOOGLE_DEVICE_CODE_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/device/code", GOOGLE_TOKEN_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token",
             GOOGLE_REVOKE_URL = "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke", GOOGLE_AUTH_URL = "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth";
/** The production wiring — the only Deps no test injects, hence spelled out here and tested as such (§12.1).
 *  `fetch` MUST be a wrapper: under workerd a bare `fetch` stored in an object is later called with `this = deps`
 *  and throws "TypeError: Illegal invocation", which `handle` would turn into 502 on every route that asks Google. */
export const defaultDeps: Deps = {
  fetch: (input, init) => fetch(input, init),
  now: () => Date.now(),
  google: { deviceCodeUrl: GOOGLE_DEVICE_CODE_URL, tokenUrl: GOOGLE_TOKEN_URL, revokeUrl: GOOGLE_REVOKE_URL, authUrl: GOOGLE_AUTH_URL },
};
export const BODY_MAX = 8192, RATE_LIMIT_RETRY_AFTER_S = 60;
/** The rate-limit key of §2.3 for a `cf-connecting-ip` value: IPv4 as it is, IPv6 as "<first four groups>::/64", null/"" → "unknown". */
export function rateLimitKey(address: string | null): string;
/** The whole Worker. Pure in (request, env, deps): no globals, no storage, no clock but `deps.now`. Never throws: unexpected errors → 500 JSON without detail. */
export async function handle(request: Request, env: Env, deps: Deps): Promise<Response>;
// ---------- src/entry.ts (0.4.0: with assets configured, wrangler refuses a main module with other named exports) ----------
export default { fetch: (request: Request, env: Env) => handle(request, env, defaultDeps) } satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>;

// ---------- src/google.ts ----------
export const SCOPES = "openid email https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file";       // what /device/start asks for; nothing a device sends can change it
export const SCOPE_DRIVE_FILE = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file";
export const ALLOWED_SCOPES: readonly string[];        // §2.2: openid, email, …/auth/userinfo.email, SCOPE_DRIVE_FILE
/** The entries of a space-separated `scope` answer outside ALLOWED_SCOPES; empty = fine. Used by /device/poll and /refresh (§2.3). */
export function excessScopes(scope: string): string[];
export const DEVICE_CODE_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_\/.~+=-]{16,512}$/, REFRESH_TOKEN_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_\/.~+=-]{20,512}$/;      // the pre-filters of §2.3
export interface Client { id: string; secret: string }
export interface Clients { device: Client; web: Client | null }     // 0.4.0 (was `legacy` / `legacyIncomplete`): `web` is null unless both GOOGLE_LEGACY_CLIENT_* secrets are set
/** null = the device pair is missing. A missing or half-set web pair is NOT null: only the hosted viewer is switched off (§2.3 "Configuration"). */
export function configuredClients(env: Env): Clients | null;
export type GoogleResult<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; status: 400 | 403 | 500 | 502; error: string; message: string };   // already mapped per §2.3
export type GoogleFailure = Exclude<GoogleResult<unknown>, { ok: true }>;
export const DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_S = 5;                                                           // RFC 8628 §3.5, when Google names no interval
/** `403 grant_unusable`: Google issued the grant (the code is consumed) and the Worker cannot hand it out. `what` completes
 *  "Google approved the sign-in, but …". Used by pollDeviceCode and by /device/poll's ID-token checks. */
export function grantUnusable(what: string): GoogleFailure;
export interface DeviceCode { device_code: string; user_code: string; verification_url: string; expires_in: number; interval: number }
/** §2.3 /device/start: client_id + SCOPES to Google's device-code endpoint; the five fields, shape-checked (`interval` absent → 5), or a mapped error. */
export async function requestDeviceCode(client: Client, deps: Deps): Promise<GoogleResult<DeviceCode>>;
export interface DeviceTokens { refresh_token: string; access_token: string; expires_in: number; scope: string; id_token: string; refresh_token_expires_in?: number }
/** §2.3 /device/poll, step 1–2: one token request for the device code. authorization_pending / slow_down / expired_token come back as
 *  status 400 under Google's own code, whatever status Google used; a token answer without refresh token, access token or ID token
 *  as 403 grant_unusable. */
export async function pollDeviceCode(client: Client, deps: Deps, deviceCode: string): Promise<GoogleResult<DeviceTokens>>;
/** `id_token` is passed through when Google sent one, for the allowlist re-check of §2.3 (done by the caller in index.ts). */
export async function refreshAccessToken(client: Client, deps: Deps, refreshToken: string): Promise<GoogleResult<{ access_token: string; expires_in: number; scope: string; id_token?: string }>>;
export async function revokeToken(deps: Deps, token: string): Promise<void>;                                                // best effort, never throws
export interface IdClaims { aud?: string; iss?: string; email?: string; email_verified?: boolean }
export function idTokenClaims(idToken: string): IdClaims | null;                                                            // payload only, no signature check (§2.3)
/** aud == the client's id and iss is Google's; used by /device/poll (else 403 grant_unusable) and by /refresh (else the id_token is ignored). */
export function claimsFromGoogle(client: Client, c: IdClaims | null): boolean;
export function emailAllowed(env: Env, c: IdClaims): boolean;                                                               // email_verified === true, the claim is printable ASCII and — ASCII case aside — a listed address
export function allowedEmails(env: Env): Set<string>;                                                                       // trimmed, ASCII letters lower-cased; empty and non-ASCII entries dropped; undefined → empty
export function maskedEmail(email: string | undefined): string | null;                                                      // "s***@example.net" for error answers; null when there is nothing presentable
export function b64urlDecode(text: string): Uint8Array | null;                                                              // null on any invalid character or length

// ---------- src/pages.ts ----------
export type Status = "ready" | "viewer_not_configured" | "not_configured";             // 0.4.0 (was "legacy_incomplete")
export const STATUS_LINE: Record<Status, string>;                                      // "Status: ready" | "Status: ready. The web viewer is not configured: it needs GOOGLE_LEGACY_CLIENT_ID,
                                                                                       // GOOGLE_LEGACY_CLIENT_SECRET and SEAL_KEY." | "Status: not configured"
export const STATUS_MARKER = "<!--gclone-status-->";                                   // 0.4.0: where the status line goes in the viewer's index.html
export const VIEWER_HEADERS: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;                         // 0.4.0: src/headers.json (§7.5)
export function viewerPage(indexHtml: string, status: Status): Response;               // 0.4.0: `/` and `/callback` — the assets' index.html with the status line, the header set, no-store
export function homePage(status: Status): Response;                                    // the fallback without viewer files: the code warning, links /privacy, the status line
export function privacyPage(): Response;
```
Rules for the code:
- **Web standard APIs only**: `fetch`, `Request`/`Response`/`URL`/`URLSearchParams`, `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder`, `AbortSignal`, and since 0.4.0 WebCrypto (`crypto.subtle`, `crypto.getRandomValues`) in `src/seal.ts` only — the sealed session, SHA-256 for PKCE and the nonce. No Node built-ins, no `cloudflare:*` import in `src/`, no npm runtime package. (0.2.0–0.3.x: no cryptography at all.)
- Stateless: no module-level mutable state; the only clock is `deps.now` (0.4.0: a session's start and end).
- Requests to Google carry `AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` and `redirect: "manual"` (the client secret is never re-sent to another address); any exception becomes `upstream_error`. `upstream_error` (502) is only ever answered where Google gave no usable answer; once a device-code poll was answered with tokens, every refusal is a 403 (§2.3).
- The request body is read only after the `Content-Type` and `Content-Length` checks, and rejected when longer than `BODY_MAX`.
- Logging: at most one `console.log(JSON.stringify({ route, status, error }))` per request. Never a body, a query string, a header, a cookie, a device code, a user code, an authorization code, a verifier or a token. `route` is one of the Worker's ten paths (§2.3) or `"other"`.
- Order of checks in `handle`: the https rule (0.4.0, §2.3) → path → method (`404` / `405`) → the pages are served here (never limited, no secrets needed) → rate limit (`env.RATE_LIMIT?.limit({ key: rateLimitKey(cf-connecting-ip) })`; an exception thrown by the binding counts as "allowed") → configuration (`500 server_misconfigured`) → `Content-Type` / size / JSON → the route's own work (the `/web/*` routes: rate limit → own-page check → configuration → body, §2.3). The pre-filters `DEVICE_CODE_RE` (in `/device/poll`) and `REFRESH_TOKEN_RE` (in `/refresh`) run before any request to Google.
- `/device/start` passes nothing of the request to Google; the web client (the former legacy client) is used by `/web/*` only — never by `/device/*`, and since 0.4.0 never by `/refresh`.
- A mapped Google error is decided by Google's `error` field, not by its HTTP status (below 500): Google answers device-code states with `428` and `403`.

Page content (wording free, these elements required; since 0.4.0 the home-page elements are also required of the viewer's sign-in screen and of the placeholder page, which replace the home page at `/`): **home** — one paragraph saying that this is the private sign-in helper of one person's gclone (encrypted file sync to their own Google Drive), that only its owner can sign in; that a sign-in starts with `gclone login` in a terminal and that a code which someone sent must never be entered (§2.3.2); a link to `/privacy`; and the status line; **privacy** — which Google data is touched (the account e-mail address, to check the allowlist; access to the Drive files gclone itself created, via `drive.file`), that the Worker stores nothing and logs no request content — only route, status and error code — and shares nothing, that Cloudflare as the hosting platform processes request metadata (IP address, time, URL path) under its own terms (the page must not claim more than this: "nothing is logged" without qualification would be false), that tokens are passed on only to the owner's own devices, and how to withdraw access (https://myaccount.google.com/permissions); since 0.4.0 also: that the service signs the owner's browser in for the web viewer, that the viewer decrypts in the browser and neither passphrase nor keys leave it, the one cookie (`__Host-gclone-web`: what it holds, that scripts cannot read it, its lifetime of 12 hours or 30 days, that Sign out removes it), and what the viewer keeps in the browser's storage (the sort order, short-lived markers of a sign-in and of an interrupted unlock; no key, nothing derived from the passphrase, no file name). There are no other pages of the Worker's own. No page loads any external resource or shows anything taken from a request, and no page, header or answer ever contains an address from `ALLOWED_EMAILS` or the address of an account that tried to sign in: the `403 email_not_allowed` answer shows that account's address masked (§2.3).

### 16.4 Google wire shapes used inside the Worker ([H]/[K], RESEARCH §6.1–§6.3; the test fake emits exactly these)
```
POST GOOGLE_DEVICE_CODE_URL (application/x-www-form-urlencoded: client_id, scope)
  success                  {"device_code":"AH-1Ng…","user_code":"GQVQ-JKEC","expires_in":1800,"interval":5,
                            "verification_url":"https://www.google.com/device"}              (verified against the real endpoint, 2026-11-12)
                           (`interval` is OPTIONAL in RFC 8628 §3.2; Google sends it. Absent → the Worker says 5, §2.3)
  quota exceeded           HTTP 403 {"error_code":"rate_limit_exceeded"}                      (no "error" field → 502 upstream_error)
  wrong client type        HTTP 401 {"error":"invalid_client", …}                             (→ 500 client_invalid)
POST GOOGLE_TOKEN_URL (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)
  device grant             grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code, device_code, client_id, client_secret
    not entered yet        HTTP 428 {"error":"authorization_pending","error_description":"Precondition Required"}
    polling too fast       HTTP 403 {"error":"slow_down","error_description":"Forbidden"}
    refused by the user    HTTP 403 {"error":"access_denied","error_description":"Forbidden"}
    code ran out           {"error":"expired_token", …}            [U]: Google's page documents no code for this; RFC 8628 names it (probe 5)
    unknown / used code    HTTP 400 {"error":"invalid_grant", …}
    success                {"access_token":"ya29.…","expires_in":3599,"refresh_token":"1//…","token_type":"Bearer",
                            "scope":"openid https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file",
                            "id_token":"<header>.<payload>.<signature>"}       + "refresh_token_expires_in":604799 for time-limited grants
                           (Google spells the granted `email` scope as …/auth/userinfo.email; every entry must be in ALLOWED_SCOPES
                            and drive.file must be among them, §2.3. The id_token: [K] from Google's "Sign-In on TVs" guide; probe 5.)
  id_token payload         {"iss":"https://accounts.google.com","aud":"<client id>","sub":"1234567890","email":"me@example.com",
                            "email_verified":true,"iat":1794400000,"exp":1794403600}
  refresh, success         {"access_token":"ya29.…","expires_in":3599,"scope":"…","token_type":"Bearer"}
                           (an id_token may be present [U]; when it is, its e-mail is re-checked against the allowlist, §2.3)
  error                    HTTP 400/401 {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"Token has been expired or revoked."}
POST GOOGLE_REVOKE_URL (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, token=<refresh or access token>)
  success                  200 {}                 error   400 {"error":"invalid_token"}
```

### 16.5 Tests
`npm test` = `vitest run`, inside the Workers runtime through the current Cloudflare integration (RESEARCH §6.5):
```ts
// worker/vitest.config.ts
import { cloudflareTest } from "@cloudflare/vitest-plugin";
import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config";
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [cloudflareTest({ wrangler: { configPath: "./wrangler.jsonc" } })],
});
```
- Tests call `handle(new Request("https://auth.test/…"), env, deps)` directly with a literal `env` (`GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: "device-cid.apps.googleusercontent.com"`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: "test-device-secret"`, `ALLOWED_EMAILS: "me@example.com"`; `withWeb()` — until 0.4.0 `withLegacy()` — adds the web client's pair and a `SEAL_KEY`) and `deps = { fetch: fakeGoogle.fetch, google: { deviceCodeUrl: "https://google.test/device/code", tokenUrl: "https://google.test/token", revokeUrl: "https://google.test/revoke" } }`. No `.dev.vars`, no bindings from the Wrangler file, no MSW, no real network: the fake `fetch` records every call and answers from a script or from the logins and tokens a test set up; an unscripted call — also a refresh with the credentials of the wrong client — fails the test.
- A full-flow test strings the routes together the way a device and its user would: `POST /device/start` → `POST /device/poll` (`authorization_pending`) → the test approves the login at the fake Google by its **user code** → `POST /device/poll` (the tokens) → `POST /refresh` with the returned refresh token and `"client": "device"`.
- **The un-injected path.** Every test above injects `deps`; the production wiring is covered by the three `defaultDeps` / default-export tests of §12.1, which must run **in the Workers runtime**: only workerd checks the `this` of `fetch`.
- The acceptance list is §12.1 (WP8). `npm run typecheck` and `npx wrangler deploy --dry-run` are part of it; `wrangler deploy` (without `--dry-run`) is not run by anyone but the user.
- (The Node fallback that §16.5 once allowed was never needed, §17.2.) A manual check before a first deploy remains possible: `wrangler dev` with `.dev.vars` serves the same code on `http://localhost:8787`, and `curl -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}' http://localhost:8787/device/start` must answer `500 client_invalid` with placeholder credentials (or `200` with real ones): Google was reached and answered — not `502 upstream_error`.

**The contract fixture `worker/test/contract.json`** — the device ↔ Worker boundary as data. WP8 writes it and proves it against the real `handle()` (`contract.test.ts`); WP3's `tests/auth.rs` reads the same file and proves `FakeDrive`'s auth routes and the Rust client against it (§12.1). It contains only what crosses that boundary: every request and answer of `/device/start`, `/device/poll` and `/refresh`, and the paths that no longer exist. Format (**version 3** since 0.4.0 — the cases of the hosted viewer's routes were added and the legacy-refresh cases removed, §16.8; version 2 since 0.2.0; version 1 was the browser-redirect contract):
```jsonc
{ "version": 3,
  "cases": [
    { "name": "poll_ok",
      "given": "approved",                               // precondition keyword, closed list below
      "request":  { "method": "POST", "path": "/device/poll", "headers": { "content-type": "application/json" },
                    "json": { "device_code": "<device_code>" } },                      // or "body": "<raw text>"
      "response": { "status": 200,
                    "headers": { "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8", "cache-control": "no-store" },   // these must be present and equal
                    "json": { "refresh_token": "<string>", "access_token": "<string>", "expires_in": "<number>",
                              "scope": "<string>", "email": "me@example.com" } } }      // EXACT key set; "<string>" / "<number>" = any value of that type
  ] }
```
`path` is relative to the auth base URL (`AUTH_URL`; `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/auth` on the fake). Header names are lower-case; a header value may be the placeholder `"<string>"` (present, any value — used for `retry-after`, where the Worker sends 60 and the fake 1). No answer may carry a `Location` header. The only keys are `method`, `path`, `headers`, `json`, `body` (request) and `status`, `headers`, `json` (response); a harness refuses anything else. Placeholders in requests, obtained by the harness from its own implementation per `given`: `<device_code>` (a login started through `/device/start`, in the state the keyword names) and `<refresh_token>`. `given` keywords — each harness maps them to its own means (the Worker's: the scripted fake Google, the fake rate limiter, `env`; the Rust side's: `FakeDrive`'s hooks) — and nothing else is allowed: `none`; for `<device_code>`: `pending` (nobody entered the code), `slow_down`, `denied`, `expired`, `used` (approved and already redeemed once), `approved`, `approved_expiring` (Google sends `refresh_token_expires_in: 604799`), `approved_other_account` (consent by an address outside the allowlist), `approved_no_drive_scope`, `approved_wide_scope` (Google granted `drive.file` **and** full `drive`), `approved_no_id_token` (Google's token answer carries no `id_token`); for `<refresh_token>`: `refresh_token` (a valid one of the device client), `refresh_revoked`, `refresh_wide_scope` (its refresh answer reports that wide scope), `legacy_token` (a valid token of the legacy client, and the legacy secrets are configured), `legacy_unconfigured` (such a token, and they are not), `legacy_half_set` (such a token, and exactly one of the two legacy secrets is set), `legacy_half_set_device_token` (a valid token of the **device** client, obtained by a login while the legacy pair is half-set); `client_broken` (Google answers `invalid_client`); `google_down` (Google answers 503); `rate_limited`; `unconfigured`.

Required cases (names are normative; WP8 may add more, WP3's harness then has to handle them; **the list is version 2's** — §16.8 names what version 3 removed and added). `/device/start`: `start_ok` (`200`, the five fields by type), `start_client_invalid` (`500`), `start_upstream` (`502`), `start_rate_limited` (`429` + `retry-after`), `start_unconfigured` (`500 server_misconfigured`), `start_wrong_content_type` (`415`), `start_get` (`405` + `allow: POST`). `/device/poll`: `poll_pending` (`400 authorization_pending`), `poll_slow_down` (`400 slow_down`), `poll_denied` (`403 access_denied`), `poll_expired` (`400 expired_token`), `poll_used` (`400 invalid_grant`), `poll_ok`, `poll_expiring` (adds `"refresh_token_expires_in": 604799`), `poll_email_not_allowed` (the consenting account is `stranger@example.com`; the message is matched literally: `"The Google account s***@example.com is not allowed to sign in here."`), `poll_scope_missing`, `poll_scope_not_allowed` (`403`), `poll_grant_unusable` (given `approved_no_id_token` → `403 grant_unusable`; on both sides the code is consumed by it), `poll_client_invalid` (`500`), `poll_upstream` (`502`), `poll_rate_limited`, `poll_unconfigured`, `poll_wrong_content_type` (`415`), `poll_too_large` (`413`), `poll_not_json`, `poll_missing_field`, `poll_malformed_code` (`400 invalid_request`), `poll_get` (`405`). `/refresh`: `refresh_ok` (body with `"client": "device"`), `refresh_legacy_ok` (given `legacy_token`, body without `client` → `200`), `refresh_legacy_unconfigured` (given `legacy_unconfigured`, body without `client` → `400 invalid_grant`), `refresh_legacy_half_set` (given `legacy_half_set`, body without `client` → `500 server_misconfigured`), `refresh_half_set_device_ok` (given `legacy_half_set_device_token`, body with `"client": "device"` → `200`), `refresh_bad_client` (`"client": "web"` → `400 invalid_request`), `refresh_invalid_grant` (`400`), `refresh_malformed_token` (`400 invalid_request`), `refresh_scope_not_allowed` (`403`), `refresh_client_invalid`, `refresh_upstream`, `refresh_rate_limited`, `refresh_unconfigured`, `refresh_get`. Elsewhere: `not_found` (`404`), and the routes of the browser sign-in — `login_gone` (`GET /login`), `callback_gone` (`GET /callback`), `token_gone` (`POST /token`) — all `404 not_found`. Error answers match as `{ "error": "<code literal>", "message": "<string>" }` (one message is a literal: `poll_email_not_allowed`). **As delivered the fixture has 48 cases**: the 46 above plus `start_not_json` and `refresh_missing_field` (`400 invalid_request`). The fake of the Rust side answers `google_down`, `rate_limited` and `unconfigured` through `fail_next` on the case's route.

### 16.6 Operating notes (go into `worker/README.md`)
- **Rotate the client secret**: Google console → the client → add a secret → `wrangler secret put GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` → delete the old one. Devices are not affected. (0.4.0: `SEAL_KEY` is replaced — never "rotated" with an overlap — to end every browser session of the hosted viewer at once: `openssl rand -base64 32 | npx wrangler secret put SEAL_KEY`. Devices are not affected.)
- **Change the allowlist**: `wrangler secret put ALLOWED_EMAILS` with the new comma-separated list — it takes effect at once, no `wrangler deploy`. Never add a `vars` entry of that name (§16.2). Removing an address stops new logins for it, and cuts off its existing tokens at their next refresh **when** Google returns an ID token there (§2.3; not guaranteed) — to be sure, revoke (`gclone logout --revoke`, or the Google account's permissions page).
- **Logs**: the Workers Logs view stores the Worker's own route / status / error code lines — a login that waits for its user therefore logs one `authorization_pending` line per poll, which is the normal state; the request URL Cloudflare attaches to each stored event has its query string removed, and invocation logs, traces and every kind of log export are off (§16.2) — do not relax any of it. `wrangler tail` prints the method and URL of every live request to the terminal of whoever runs it; bodies are not shown, and one URL carries a secret since 0.4.0 — a browser sign-in shows as `GET /callback?code=…&state=…` with Google's single-use authorization code. Requests for the viewer's static files do not run the Worker and write no line. Cloudflare still sees request metadata at the platform level (the privacy page says so).
- **Cost and limits**: a login is one start plus one poll every 5 s while the user enters the code (about 13 requests for a minute at Google), a refresh 1 per device and hour of use — far inside the Workers free plan (100,000 requests/day) for the owner's own use. The built-in rate limit (30 requests / 60 s per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64, `429`) bounds what one sender can relay to Google through the OAuth client — not a sender with many networks — and it runs inside the Worker: a refused request is still a request, so on `*.workers.dev` a flood of about one request per second uses up the free plan's daily quota and stops all token refreshes until midnight UTC — and zone-level rate-limiting rules cannot be attached to `*.workers.dev`. **Recommended**: serve the Worker from a custom domain (a zone on the same Cloudflare account), attached **in `wrangler.jsonc`** — `"routes": [{ "pattern": "<host>", "custom_domain": true }]` with `"workers_dev": false` (and the shipped `"preview_urls": false`) — so that every deploy, and a redeploy of a lost Worker, restores the host name the devices and the Google branding depend on; a domain attached only in the dashboard is not restored. In the Google console add, under *Authorized domains*, the **registrable domain** of the host (`example.org` for `auth.example.org`; Google refuses a subdomain there — `setup.sh` prints it that way); use `https://<host>` as `AUTH_URL`; and add one zone rate-limiting rule. **The rule must cover every path of the host** (§17.14), not the three limited routes: `/`, `/privacy` and every unknown path invoke the Worker as well (the two pages and `404` are answered before the limiter) and count against the quota like any other request — a rule for `/device/start`, `/device/poll`, `/refresh` alone leaves the flood of §1.3 exactly as possible as before. Per IP address, action Block, **5 requests per 10 seconds** (a login that waits polls once every 5 s — 2 requests per 10 s — and a blocked poll only delays it; 10 at most — the 20 per 10 s once given as the example admits 172,800 requests a day from one address, more than the whole free quota). The expression depends on the zone's plan [K, Cloudflare's rate-limiting documentation, read 2026-11]: Pro and above can match the host (`http.host eq "<host>"`); the Free plan has one rule whose expression can use the URI path only, with a 10 s period and a 10 s block, so there the rule is zone-wide (`starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/")`) — right for a zone that serves nothing but the Worker, too strict for one that also serves a site; on such a zone only a zone of its own for the Worker, the Pro plan or the paid Workers plan help. Requests blocked by the rule never reach the Worker and do not count; the device treats the `429` like the Worker's own (§17.3). A per-address rule bounds each sender (43,200 requests a day at 5 per 10 s), **not the total**: a flood from many addresses can still exhaust the free quota, and only the paid plan, which has no daily cap, removes that. The custom domain is best chosen **before the first deploy** (§2.1): `setup.sh` asks, and `scripts/custom-domain.mjs <host>` writes the `routes` entry. **With the hosted viewer (0.4.0)** the rule becomes 10 requests per 10 seconds over every path **except** the static files — `not starts_with(http.request.uri.path, "/a/") and http.request.uri.path ne "/sw.js"` — which do not run the Worker and would otherwise make one page load (about twenty requests) trip the rule; what is left counts 2 requests for a page load and 5 for a sign-in. Whether the Free plan's rule builder accepts that expression is [U]. The zone setting "Always Use HTTPS" must be on: it is what keeps the static files from being served over plain `http` (the Worker's own `308` never runs for them).
- **If the Worker is lost**: redeploy from `worker/` and put the three secrets again (a new client secret can be added to the same Google client). Devices keep their refresh tokens; nothing else needs to change as long as the host name and the Google client stay the same — with a custom domain that means: as long as its `routes` entry is in `wrangler.jsonc` (or the domain is attached again in the dashboard).

### 16.7 What the Worker deliberately does not do
No storage and no session list (Google holds a pending login, the device its device code, the browser its sealed cookie — §2.3.1); no cookie on any device route; no CORS; no redirect but `http` → `https` (the browser's trip to Google is a navigation by the page to an address the Worker only formats); no confirmation step against device-code phishing (§2.3.2) — the hosted viewer's page is not one: the device flow never passes through it; nothing about the owner disclosed to an unauthenticated caller; no proxying of Drive traffic (data never passes through it); no revoke endpoint (devices call Google's directly — it needs no client secret); no user management beyond the e-mail allowlist; no verification of ID-token signatures (the token comes straight from Google's token endpoint over TLS); no request logging beyond route, status and error code; no token for a grant with any scope beyond `ALLOWED_SCOPES`; no cryptography but the sealed browser session (0.4.0); no revoke on sign-out of the viewer (it would sign every device out); no refresh of a web-client token outside its sealed cookie.

### 16.8 The hosted viewer's side of the Worker (0.4.0, §17.22)

What §7.5 needs from the Worker: the page, the four sign-in routes, the static files. The HTTP contract is §2.3; this subsection fixes files, configuration and tooling.

**Source.**
```ts
// ---------- src/web.ts ----------
export const WEB_COOKIE = "__Host-gclone-web", WEB_SESSION_TTL_S = 12 * 3600, WEB_SESSION_REMEMBER_TTL_S = 30 * 86400;
export const CLEAR_COOKIE: string;                                                    // "__Host-gclone-web=; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=0"
export interface WebConfig { client: Client; sealKey: Uint8Array }                    // the web client and the decoded SEAL_KEY
export interface WebCtx { request: Request; origin: string; env: Env; deps: Deps; web: WebConfig }
export function fromOwnPage(request: Request, origin: string): boolean;               // Origin == origin, and Sec-Fetch-Site (if sent) == "same-origin"
export async function webStart(ctx: WebCtx, body: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<Reply>;
export async function webToken(ctx: WebCtx, body: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<Reply>;
export async function webRefresh(ctx: WebCtx): Promise<Reply>;
export function webLogout(): Reply;
// ---------- src/seal.ts (WebCrypto only: runs unchanged under workerd and under Node >= 20) ----------
export function decodeSealKey(text: unknown): Uint8Array | null;                      // base64 or base64url of exactly 32 bytes, else null
export interface WebSession { iat: number; exp: number; email: string; refreshToken: string }
export async function sealSession(sealKey: Uint8Array, s: WebSession): Promise<string>;                       // the blob of §2.3
export async function openSession(sealKey: Uint8Array, blob: string, nowS: number): Promise<WebSession | null>;   // null: another key, damaged, a pre-0.2.0 kind, expired
export async function pkceChallenge(verifier: string): Promise<string>;               // base64url(SHA-256(verifier))
export async function loginNonce(challenge: string): Promise<string>;                 // base64url(SHA-256("gclone-auth/v2/nonce" ‖ challenge))
export const SESSION_BLOB_MAX = 805, SESSION_BLOB_MAX_CHARS = 1074;
// ---------- src/google.ts, added ----------
export function authorizationUrl(client: Client, deps: Deps, redirectUri: string, challenge: string, state: string, nonce: string): string;
export async function exchangeCode(client: Client, deps: Deps, redirectUri: string, code: string, verifier: string): Promise<GoogleResult<DeviceTokens>>;
// ---------- src/reply.ts: the JSON answers (moved out of index.ts) ----------
export interface Reply { response: Response; error?: string }
// ---------- src/index.ts, added in 0.5.0 (§17.27) ----------
export const SERVICE_WORKER_PATH = "/sw.js", CLEAR_SITE_DATA = '"cache", "storage"';
```
`src/headers.json` is the header set of §7.5 as a flat `{name: value}` object, read by `src/pages.ts` and by `scripts/headers-file.mjs`, whose `headersFile()` writes the text of `dist/_headers` (two rules, `/a/*` and `/sw.js`, each with the whole set). `idTokenClaims` keeps `nonce`. The former `Clients.legacy` is `Clients.web`.

**Static assets.** `wrangler.jsonc`'s `assets` entry (§16.2) uploads `worker/dist/` (git-ignored): `index.html` (read by the Worker only, for `/` and `/callback`; the marker `<!--gclone-status-->` exactly once), `sw.js`, `_headers`, `a/<16 hex>/…` with `manifest.json` (§7.5). Measured under `wrangler dev` 4.160.1 (`scripts/smoke.mjs`; production is expected to behave the same and is unverified): `/a/<build>/*` and `/sw.js` come from the asset layer with the `_headers` rules, Cloudflare's default `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` and an `ETag` (`If-None-Match` → `304`), **without the Worker running** — no log line; a miss under `/a/` is an empty `404`, a `POST` there `405`, both from the asset layer; `/index.html`, `/_headers`, `/a`, `/A/…`, `/sw.js/` and `/v/…` reach the Worker and get its JSON `404`. Without a built viewer, `scripts/stub-dist.mjs` writes a **placeholder** of the same layout (a static page with the home-page text and the status line, a `sw.js` that handles nothing, `_headers`, `a/0000000000000000/` with a stylesheet and a manifest that says `"stub": true`); it never touches a `dist/` that holds anything else, and a Worker deployed with it is the plain sign-in helper. With no assets binding or no `index.html` at all, `/` and `/callback` are the Worker's own home page (`200`, the status line).

**A Service Worker that is not the viewer's** (0.5.0, §17.27; the audit's L6). The honest deployment registers one Service Worker, `/sw.js`, which the asset layer serves. A request that reaches the Worker with `Service-Worker: script` — what a browser sends when it installs a Service Worker or checks one for an update — for **any other path** therefore comes from a registration that someone else made while they served this origin (§1.3, the Cloudflare row), or that an earlier use of the domain left. `handle()` answers it as the path is answered (`404` for a path without a route) and adds `Clear-Site-Data: "cache", "storage"` — not `"cookies"`, which would clear the registrable domain. `Sec-Fetch-Dest`, when sent, must be `serviceworker`: Firefox sends `Service-Worker: script` also for the scripts a Service Worker *imports* (with `Sec-Fetch-Dest: script`), the viewer's Service Worker imports its files from `/a/<build>/`, and a file that a deployment has not propagated yet must not clear anything. Nobody can make a browser send the header from another site (it is not a simple header; no answer carries CORS), and a script of the origin itself could clear the same data without it. **What it achieves, measured** (Chrome 157, Playwright's WebKit 27.2 and Firefox 159, over `http://127.0.0.1`; not on a deployment): Chrome drops the registration, the storage and the cache when the answer arrives — at the registration's next update check, so the visit that triggers it still shows the other party's page; Firefox does not act on `Clear-Site-Data` in the answer to a Service Worker's script at all (it does on a page's own requests); WebKit cleared the storage and **kept the registration**, on every kind of request. And it reaches only paths that run the Worker: a miss under `/a/` is the asset layer's `404` (`scripts/smoke.mjs`), so a script planted there — with a `Service-Worker-Allowed` header to give it the whole origin — is never asked of the Worker; a foreign script at `/sw.js` itself needs no switch (the update check finds the release's bytes and installs them). It is an aid for the commonest browser, not the remedy, which is clearing the site's data by hand.

**Local development.** `npm run dev` is `wrangler dev --upstream-protocol https`: by default `wrangler dev` 4.160.1 hands the Worker `http://<route host>/…`, and the https rule would answer every page with a redirect; with the flag the Worker sees `https://<route host>/…`, and wrangler maps the browser's local `Origin` to that origin.

**Scripts** (plain Node; the first five use Node built-ins and `gh` only, no npm package — §7.5 says what each guarantees):

| Script | Does |
|---|---|
| `scripts/check-dist.mjs [dir] [--release <tag>]` | the rules of a deployable `dist/`; exports `inspectDist`, `checkDist` |
| `scripts/release-bundle.mjs` | `releaseBundle(tag)`: download the tag's `gclone-viewer-<version>.tar.gz`, `gh attestation verify` it, unpack with its own reader, `check-dist --release`. The repository is `GCLONE_REPO`, else the one `install.sh` uses |
| `scripts/fetch-viewer.mjs <tag> [--dist <dir>]` | replaces `dist/` with the verified bundle; refuses a `dist/` that holds anything but a bundle or the placeholder |
| `scripts/check-release.mjs [dir]` | the gate of `npm run deploy`: `dist/` is byte for byte the attested bundle of the tag its manifest names |
| `scripts/verify-deployed.mjs https://<host> <tag>` (or `--dist <dir>`) | compares what a host serves with the release (or a local build) |
| `scripts/smoke.mjs` | `wrangler dev` on `dist/` twice (as `https://viewer.example` and as `http://viewer.example`, made-up secrets, only routes that answer without asking Google): the routing and header table above, the https rule, `check-dist`, and `verify-deployed`'s comparison |
| `viewer/build.mjs [--out <dir>] [--pkg <dir>]` | the bundle (§7.5) |

`npm run deploy` = `check-config && check-release && wrangler deploy`; `npm run deploy:dev` = `check-config && stub-dist && check-dist --not-a-release && wrangler deploy` (one line says what is deployed). No test, script or workflow deploys.

**Tests.** `test/seal.test.ts` (round trip; a flipped byte; another key; expiry; a blob of the pre-0.2.0 kinds is refused; size bounds) and `test/web.test.ts` (the exact authorization URL; cookie attributes; no refresh token in any body; `remember`; another tab's verifier; a code from a URL the Worker did not build; an address off the allowlist; a grant that is too wide; cross-origin and missing `Origin`; refresh with no, a tampered, a foreign-key and an expired cookie; allowlist removal; Google down (cookie kept) against token dead (cookie cleared); logout; `/` ≡ `/callback` with the header set and no echo; one log line per request; the https rule; since 0.5.0 `Clear-Site-Data` for a foreign Service Worker's script and for nothing else — `test/refresh.test.ts`), in workerd. **`test/contract.json` version 3**: removed `refresh_legacy_ok`, `refresh_legacy_unconfigured`, `refresh_legacy_half_set`, `callback_gone` and the givens `legacy_unconfigured`, `legacy_half_set`; added `refresh_no_client` and `refresh_legacy_gone` (a body without `client` → `400 invalid_grant`, with and without the web client configured) and 34 cases for `/`, `/callback` and `/web/*`, with 14 `web…` givens and the placeholders `<origin>`, `<challenge>`, `<state>`, `<code>`, `<verifier>`, `<cookie>`; a case may now expect `set-cookie` (only on `/web/token`, `/web/refresh`, `/web/logout`). The Rust side (`tests/auth.rs`) checks the browser cases for their shape only — `FakeDrive` does not serve them — and keeps, annotated, the tests that model a 0.2–0.3.x Worker with legacy secrets. The scripts' own tests (`scripts/*.selftest.mjs`, `node --test`): `check-config` (the new rules, each with a failing example), `stub-dist` and `headers-file`, `check-dist`, and the release tooling against a stand-in `gh`. As delivered: 229 tests in workerd, 52 in Node, `smoke.mjs` 349 checks on a built bundle.
