Only the opposite direction had been handled. **A passphrase is set to exactly the text gclone 0.4.0 makes of the same input** (`Passphrase::for_setting`, behind `set_checked`); it is entered with both readings (`readings()`), canonical first. A generated passphrase is unchanged — it is set in the canonical form, which is one text for every version, and entered in any spelling from 0.5.0 on; a typed one of the shape is exact in spelling, as every typed passphrase is, and `login` / `passwd` say so once when it is set. Tests: `tests/crypto_format.rs::a_passphrase_is_set_to_what_gclone_0_4_0_makes_of_it` (the frozen 0.4.0 vectors, and 130 spellings against an independent re-implementation of the 0.4.0 normalisation), `tests/cli_e2e.rs::passphrase_rules`; and by hand with the 0.4.0 binary (**Results**).
2. *The right passphrase after a mis-cased attempt was answered "Wrong passphrase" without a derivation.* `login`'s memo of refused passphrases was keyed by the canonical form, which two spellings share; the keyfile was sealed under one of them as typed. The memo is per reading, and only the readings a keyfile has not refused are derived. Test: `cli::login::tests::the_right_spelling_opens_after_a_miscased_attempt` (two derivations for the wrong spelling, none for its repetition, one for the right one).

**`gclone passwd` (§2.7).**

3. *Ctrl-C at the purge question left the old passphrase in force for good, under the words "Passphrase changed"* (two reports). The question of §17.26 item 6 was asked after the new keyfile was written and announced, with the retirement of the old one waiting for the answer. **The question is asked before anything is written**; put and retirement follow each other without a pause; "Passphrase changed." is printed after the retirement; a retirement that fails says that the old keyfile is still in the vault folder and still works. With `--passphrase-file` nothing is asked (as in `login`). `gclone check` warns when the vault folder holds more than one object under a keyfile's name — what a `passwd` killed between the two steps leaves. Tests: `tests/cli_e2e.rs::an_interrupt_at_the_purge_question_of_passwd_changes_nothing` (a pseudo-terminal, `^C` typed at the question: nothing written, nothing said, the old passphrase is the passphrase), `passwd_can_delete_the_old_keyfiles_for_good`, `passwd_writes_a_new_keyfile`.
4. *`passwd --purge-old` said "gone … trash included" while keyfiles of old passphrases were in the trash.* The trash was purged below the new generation only, and the generation was counted from the listed keyfiles: with the current keyfile moved to the trash by hand, the new one got generation 1 again and every trashed keyfile survived. **With `purge`, every object under a keyfile's name in the trash is deleted, whatever its generation; the generation counts the trash too; and "gone" is said only when a listing made afterwards shows it.** Tests: `tests/cli_e2e.rs::passwd_purge_old_empties_the_trash_of_keyfiles_whatever_their_generation`, `tests/index_props.rs::retired_keyfiles_can_be_deleted_for_good_trash_included` (whose expectation for a trashed keyfile of an equal or higher generation is now "deleted"), `cli::passwd::tests::gone_is_said_only_when_a_listing_shows_it`.

**The index (§5.2.2, §5.3).**

5. *`restore` brought back the wrong version when a writer's clock was ahead.* §17.26 item 3 made `removed_ms` the later of the store's time and the time the writer sealed — from its own clock — and versions were ordered by `removed_ms`. A device three days ahead overwrote a file; the next overwrite, by a device on the right clock, sorted as older; `gclone restore PATH` returned the version before last and listed a removal date in the future. 0.4.0, on the store's clock alone, ordered correctly. **Versions are ordered by the superseding op's stamp** (`by`: causal), in `removed_versions`, `removed_under` and `restore_many`; `removed_ms` bounds the windows and nothing else; and **`SegmentV1.created_ms` is sealed from the store-synchronised clock** (`backend.now_ms()`), so that an honest device with a wrong clock neither dates its removals into the future nor, with a clock behind, leaves them to the store's time (the L5 hole for that writer). Tests: `tests/index_props.rs::removed_versions_are_ordered_by_the_superseding_op_not_by_time` (replicas that applied one by one, at once, and from a snapshot agree), `tests/sync_e2e.rs::restore_orders_versions_causally_when_a_writer_clock_is_ahead`; and the reviewer's two-binary script under libfaketime (**Results**).
6. *An object listed without an md5 passed for the accepted one* (low). `same_bytes` took "the right size, no md5" for a match, in presence rules (a) and (c), the base-on-offer test and `repair`. On Drive that is a Google-native file, which a `drive.file` token can create under an index object's name; whether Drive can be made to report a chosen size for one was not tried (no real Drive was contacted) — a gap in the L4 fix, not a demonstrated bypass. **`same_bytes` needs a reported, equal md5; an object without one is judged by its content, read once** (`Vault::is_object`, `find_object`, the BLAKE3 comparison of `holds_segment`), and one that cannot be read is not it. Tests: `tests/index_adversary.rs` — the md5-less plant as a third attack in `a_segment_replaced_under_its_own_name_is_a_rollback_for_those_who_applied_it`, the whole index replaced by md5-less objects in `the_whole_index_replaced_under_the_same_names_is_a_rollback`, and `a_genuine_object_listed_without_an_md5_is_judged_by_its_content`; `MemBackend::strip_md5`; the fake Drive's `make_native` with `tests/drive_http.rs::a_google_native_file_has_a_size_no_md5_and_no_content`.

**The hosted viewer (§1.3, §7.5).**

7. *The security statement was too kind about Lock and the passphrase, and one statement of a script kept a tab from ever locking.* `lock()` set its "leaving" flag, assigned `document.body.hidden`, and only then told the Service Worker to forget, ended the vault worker and reloaded: a script that made that assignment throw kept all three from happening, and — the flag being set — every later Lock, the lock by the clock, another tab's lock and Sign out returned at once; the vault worker went on issuing tickets for as long as the tab lived, and the script could answer the Lock click with the page's own unlock screen and read what was typed. **Code**: the irreversible steps come first, each in its own `try`, with `ServiceWorker.prototype.postMessage` and `Worker.prototype.terminate` taken when the scripts loaded (`shell.js`, `provider.js`); `signOut` sends its request and reloads whatever its other steps do. **Statement** (§1.3 row, §7.5, §17.27, `docs/AUTH.md`, `README.md`): a script in the unlocked page can keep that tab from locking or signing out and then keeps the open vault for as long as the tab lives; it has the passphrase the next time it is typed or filled into that tab; the seal's gain is stated for a script that is gone before the passphrase is entered again; and the advice — if in doubt, close the tab or the browser rather than pressing Lock, and do not enter the passphrase in that tab again. The hardening does not replace the statement: a script can still keep a lock from being asked for. Test: step `unskippable` of `worker/test/e2e/run.mjs` (the Lock button, the clock, another tab's lock and Sign out, each with `document.body.hidden` throwing and `ServiceWorker.postMessage`, `Worker.terminate`, `history.replaceState` and `Storage.setItem` replaced: a new document, no ticket, no port, the session gone at the Worker).
8. *A second registration of `/sw.js` took the vault worker over and read files after the Lock* (low). `/sw.js` behaved as the viewer's Service Worker under any scope, and `forget` goes to the page's controller. **An instance that is not registered for the whole origin is inert and removes itself** (`sw.js`: decided before `importScripts`). Test: step `second` (the registration list stays `['/']`, the key the vault worker seals to is unchanged, a window inside the second scope reads nothing after the Lock); step `planted` now expects the planted registration to remove itself.
9. *After the Service Worker lost its tickets, all but the last of several files asked for at once answered `410`* (low; not new, but the seal turned a race into a certainty in Chrome and WebKit). A ticket was posted on the port that was current when it was asked for. **`issue()` seals for, and posts on, the channel that is current when the ticket is ready.** The extra 200 ms for the second and later files of a tab whose start-up seal went stale remain. Test: step `recover` (three files at once after another tab made the Service Worker forget, three rounds, and in Chrome after `ServiceWorker.stopAllWorkers`: all `206`).

**The key store (§8.1, §8.2).**

10. *`gclone login` could destroy the only device copy of the vault key on a sealed device* (high). An enclave that fails once makes every command say "the stored key cannot be used any more … Run `gclone login`"; that login treats the failed open as "no usable secrets", signs in, and saves the grant **without a key** before it asks for the passphrase — and `save_with`, looking at the files again, found a sealed file that opened by then and re-sealed the keyless document over it. A wrong, forgotten or abandoned passphrase left the device locked; two unit fixtures used that very save. **Sealed keys are never replaced by a document without keys** (rule 3, the save table): the keyless login goes to `secrets.json` beside the sealed file — the merged view — and the one exception, `save_dropping_keys`, names the keys it gives up (the vault that lost a creation race). **A stored key that fails while a new key works is tried once more** before anything is said. Tests: `keystore::tests::a_keyless_save_never_replaces_sealed_keys`, `tests/cli_e2e.rs::drive_mode_a_transient_enclave_failure_during_login_keeps_the_sealed_key` (the fake Drive; the stand-in's new `open-first-N` mode; a wrong passphrase and an abandoned prompt — the sealed file is byte for byte what it was and the device works); both fail with the rule taken out. Not observed: a real Secure Enclave failing once.
11. *`gclone keystore` credited the trial's evidence to a key that was never on trial.* When the trial's test value did not open at the move, a new key took the secrets, and the record was marked "moved" all the same. The record keeps the public half of its key; **whether the trial's key holds the secrets is read off the two files**, and where it does not, `keystore`, `status` and `--json` say so. Tests: `keystore::tests::a_move_to_a_new_key_is_not_reported_as_the_trials_key`, `tests/keystore.rs::a_move_that_could_not_use_the_trials_key_never_borrows_its_evidence`.
12. *"No Secure Enclave on this machine" on a Mac whose enclave works* (low). A first step in a session that could not make a key was recorded without the session and retried only after another boot, another system version or seven days. **The session is recorded, another session retries at once, the line names the session and its date, and the trial that then starts keeps the failure.** Tests: `keystore::trial::tests::a_session_that_cannot_make_a_key_speaks_for_itself_alone`, `tests/keystore.rs::a_session_that_cannot_make_a_key_is_not_the_machine`.
13. *The trial's step ran inline in every command, without a time bound* (low). Whether Security.framework can block in a session nobody measured is not known; that nothing in gclone bounded it was shown with the stand-in. **The step runs on its own thread, awaited for two seconds; a step that does not return is a recorded failure, and that boot and session are left alone for a day.** The opt-outs are unchanged (`gclone keystore use file`, `GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0`). Tests: `keystore::trial::tests::a_step_that_does_not_return_is_given_up_and_not_repeated`, the `hang` case of `keystore::tests::the_trial_runs_from_load_on_the_plain_file_and_never_changes_the_answer`, `tests/keystore.rs::a_trial_step_that_hangs_delays_one_command_by_a_bounded_time`.
14. *The once-only note about older backups was lost when first runs overlapped* (low). "Owed" was a member of the trial's record, which every process rewrote from its own stale copy; the exclusion attribute was set by then, so the note never became due again. **The owed note is a marker file created with `O_EXCL` and consumed by its removal; every change of the trial's record is a read-change-write under a kernel lock** (which also keeps failure entries). Tests: `tests/keystore.rs::the_backup_note_survives_first_runs_that_overlap_without_a_terminal` (macOS; eight processes at once, six rounds), `keystore::trial::tests::a_step_writes_into_the_record_as_it_is_now`.
15. *A plain copy of the secrets could stay beside a sealed store unseen; an interrupted `use file` was not put right by `use enclave`; losers of concurrent moves were told their login had changed* (low). **Every save removes the temp copies of killed writes under its lock; `status` and `keystore` count them and warn; `keystore use enclave` on a sealed device settles them and the choice file; a move that finds the secrets sealed already says so.** Tests: `keystore::tests::a_plain_temp_copy_of_the_secrets_is_reported_and_removed_by_the_next_save`, `a_move_that_finds_the_secrets_sealed_already_says_so`, `tests/keystore.rs::leftovers_beside_a_sealed_store_are_reported_and_settled` (six `use enclave` at once: one moves, none says "login changed").

**Releases and the installer (§17.28).**

16. *A draft left by an interrupted upload was refused forever.* `gh release upload --clobber` deletes the old asset, then uploads. **`SHA256SUMS` is derived from the attested archives**; the draft may lack it, the signed archive, or both. Tests: the cases "the upload of SHA256SUMS is cut off …", "… of the signed archive …", "a draft with the attested archives and nothing else" of `tests/release/selftest.sh`; `fake-gh.sh` models `--clobber` as delete-then-upload, with a `cut-upload` hook.
17. *Step 16 turned any failed gh call into "cannot be repaired … publish a new patch release", with no way to look again.* **Each question is retried, gh's words are kept, "could not be verified yet" is told apart from "does not verify", and `--verify-published <tag>` verifies a published release from GitHub alone.** Tests: the cases "step 16: one transient error …", "… keeps failing", "--verify-published …" (five of them).
18. *Step 8 (continuity) failed open when gh failed*, and announced the first signed release. **Both calls fail closed.** Tests: the two "continuity: gh … fails" cases.
19. *The "no entitlements" check read a failed query as "none"*, in `install.sh` and in the release script. **codesign's exit status counts.** Tests: "step 7 refuses when the entitlements cannot be read"; in `tests/install/test.sh` "signed build: codesign cannot report the entitlements" (a `codesign` on `PATH` that refuses `--entitlements`).
20. *The release script depended on Apple's `tar`, `file`, `otool`, `lipo` from `PATH`*, and refused an attested binary inside the project's nix shell. **The system directories come first on its `PATH`.** Test: "other tools of the same names first on PATH"; the self-test also passes inside `nix-shell -p cargo rustc`.
21. *`install.sh` assumed a gh newer than the one it probed for*: `--source-ref` (gh 2.68.0) and `gh release verify-asset` (2.75.0), behind a probe that only showed 2.49.0 — an older gh made every install fail with a false statement about the release. **Both are probed; an older gh is called too old, by its number.** Tests: five cases with `FAKE_GH_AGE=2.67` and `2.74`.
22. *The documented release-day order left hours in which the README's one-liner refused for everyone with a signed-in gh.* The one-liner pipes `install.sh` from `main`; the new `install.sh` refuses a latest release without attested binaries; and the draft flow keeps v0.4.0 "latest" until the owner has signed. **The tag is pushed alone, `main` after the release is published** (README "Publishing a release" and its status paragraph, `worker/README.md` "Release-day order", §17.28; the script's last line says it). Documentation only.

**Deviations from what the reviewers proposed**, each on purpose: (a) item 1 takes the "stronger alternative" (seal as typed) *and* the notice, not the notice alone — the task's constraint is that old and new binaries interoperate; (b) item 11 passes no flag into the move: the record keeps the public half and the report compares it with the sealed file's, so a record cannot claim what the files do not show; (c) item 14 does both of the alternatives offered (the marker *and* the lock), because the lost update also dropped failure entries; (d) item 6 reads an md5-less object instead of refusing it outright, so that a store which reported no md5 for genuine objects would not be a permanent false alarm (none of gclone's does); (e) `--verify-published` and the two outcomes of step 16 have different exit statuses (3 and 1).

**Results** (macOS 27.2, Apple silicon; cargo and rustc 1.99.0 from nix; Node 24.21; restic on `PATH` and `GCLONE_REQUIRE_RESTIC=1`; `GCLONE_DEFAULT_AUTH_URL` unset). `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --locked` — **895 passed, 3 ignored** (873 before this entry: lib 413, `auth` 29, `backend_conformance` 37, `cli_e2e` 38, `cross_package` 14, `crypto_format` 41, `drive_http` 45, `index_adversary` 22, `index_props` 65, `keystore` 18, `restic_e2e` 26, `restic_http` 10, `sync_e2e` 55, `sync_faults` 16, `transfer` 42, `web` 24) — and `tests/keystore.rs` once more with `GCLONE_TEST_OLD_GCLONE` naming a gclone built from the tag v0.4.0 (18 passed, the old-binary test among them); `cargo build --release --locked`, without a warning. `web-core/`: `cargo fmt --check`, clippy for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and for the host, `tests/parity.rs` 19, the module built again (four imports, all wasm-bindgen's), `web-core/test/run.sh` with its browser smoke test in the three engines. `worker/`: `npm run typecheck`; `npm test` 56 + 239; `npm run test:viewer` 45; the bundle built, `check-dist` ok, `npm run smoke` 375 checks. The browser suite with the 48.8 MiB fixture, `node worker/test/e2e/run.mjs chrome webkit firefox`: Chrome 157, Playwright WebKit 27.2 and Firefox 159 all OK, the steps `unskippable`, `second` and `recover` among them (each of the three fails against the bundle built before this entry: `recover` with `[[410,3212],[410,3212],[206,213]]`, `second` with "a second registration of /sw.js stayed", `unskippable` by never reaching the unlock screen); `signin.mjs` and `local.mjs` OK. `tests/install/test.sh`: 111 cases under `sh` and under `bash`. `tests/release/selftest.sh`: 58 cases, outside and inside `nix-shell -p cargo rustc`. `shellcheck` on every script of the CI job and `actionlint`: clean. *With the 0.4.0 binary beside the new one* (directory vaults, isolated homes): a vault created by 0.5.0 with the typed passphrase `the new victim passphrase long` — a 0.4.0 device logs in with the same file (it answered "Wrong passphrase", exit 4, before); `passwd` on 0.5.0 to that passphrase in a vault that 0.4.0 created — a fresh 0.4.0 device logs in; and a passphrase of that shape set by 0.4.0 opens on 0.5.0. *Two devices, one of them under libfaketime at +3 days*: `restore --list` now shows the version the fast device wrote as K 1 and `gclone restore` brings it back, as 0.4.0 does (before: the version before last). In a directory vault the fast device's removal still carries its own date — there the machine's clock is the store's.

**Not verified.** Linux: nothing of this entry was compiled or run on Linux (no container was at hand in this session); the changed code has no new platform-specific part outside `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` — the backup note — but that it builds warning-free there is an expectation, to be shown by CI. A real Secure Enclave that fails once (item 10) or blocks (item 13): both are injected with the stand-in; the sealed-store tests with the real enclave ran as before. Drive itself: whether a Google-native file can be given a chosen size (item 6), and everything gh and GitHub do in the release script — the self-test's fake models `--clobber` as gh 2.103's source has it (delete, then upload), and `--verify-published` has never met a real release. The viewer's hardening was run in Chrome, Playwright's WebKit and Firefox on macOS; not in Safari itself and not on a phone. A password manager that fills login forms without a click (item 7's remark in `docs/AUTH.md`) was not tried.

### 17.30 gclone 0.5.1 — the sealed store is a Mac's default: tested, then used, without a command (2026-11-14)

**The owner's decision**, on reading what 0.5.0 had built (§17.28: the plain file stays until the owner runs `gclone keystore use enclave`, which asks for the passphrase): *"it would be good if we test SE and then that's just the default for all users."* No command and no interaction: gclone tests the Secure Enclave by itself and, when the test passes, `secrets.sealed` is simply what a Mac uses. This reverses one decision of §17.28 — "automatic removal of `secrets.json` after a trial" was cut there as "the one step that can lock a device out" — and this entry says what was built instead, which of the old objections are met and which are accepted. **No format changed**: `secrets.json`, `secrets.sealed`, `keystore.json` and `keystore-trial.json` are what 0.5.0 reads and writes (two new empty marker files, `keystore-note.due` and `keystore-trial.off`, and one new optional member of the trial's record, `last_ok_ms`, which 0.5.0 ignores and this version writes again after a 0.5.0 run dropped it); a 0.5.0 trial record counts; gclone 0.5.0 works on a device that 0.5.1 sealed. Linux is untouched.

Edited in place: the title line, §1.3 (the row of the unlocked device), §2.5, §2.8, §7.1, §7.3, §8.1–§8.3, §9.2, §9.10, §13 (item 8d), §14 (item 4), §15; `README.md` ("Status", "Upgrading to 0.5.1", "Security model in brief", "Where a device keeps its key", "Limitations", "Local files", "Development"), `docs/AUTH.md` ("What lives where", "Where the refresh token lives on a device"), `worker/README.md` (version examples).

**What was built** (§8.2 is the specification).
1. **A login seals from the start.** The save table's row "neither file" seals by default: `keystore::pick_key` takes the trial's key if its test value opens, else makes a key that seals 16 bytes and opens them in this process (awaited two seconds on a thread of its own); `envelope_for` seals the document and opens the ciphertext in memory; `write_sealed` reads the file back. No `secrets.json` is written — for a Drive vault from the first, keyless save on. **Fallback, silent**: no sealer (Linux, a debug build), no key, nothing opens, a seal that does not round-trip, a call that does not return, a failure on this Mac's trial record → `secrets.json`, a debug-level log line, and the reason written into the trial's record so that `status` and `keystore` show it in one line. (After the review, below: also a trial that is running and has not passed — then `status` shows the trial's progress.)
2. **A device on the plain file is tested and then moved.** The trial of 0.5.0 is the test, unchanged; `keystore::automatic_move` runs from `after_load` in the run that took the step, under the six conditions of §8.2, and calls the one move sequence with `MoveBy::Trial`. One note, on a terminal or owed.
3. **The end of a login** moves what the save table sent to the plain file on a Mac whose default is the sealed store (a sealed file that did not open; a merged view) — `MoveBy::Login` — unless the device was working from a keyed `secrets.json` before, or (after the review) a trial was running there that had not passed.
4. **A sealed store that does not open** says "This Mac's Secure Enclave cannot open this device's sealed key (secrets.sealed) … Run `gclone login` … connects this device again", exit 4 as before, and the login it asks for ends sealed on the Mac it runs on. The session text gained the way out that needs no login: `gclone keystore use file` from a session where the enclave works.
5. **Opt-outs**: `gclone keystore use file` (remembered; the automatic move looks at the choice again under the lock), `GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0` (per run: no step, no move, no sealing login — and, after the review, for the whole device through the marker such a run leaves). `gclone keystore use enclave` is unchanged and is now "at once" / "opt back in".

**The bar: three days, a restart, no failure — kept.** The reasons are in §8.2 ("The bar"); in short: the restart is what no in-process test shows and what §17.28 left unmeasured; the days give a daily job in its own session the chance to fail first; one failure stops the move for good; waiting costs a device that has always been on the plain file almost nothing, and every 0.5.0 Mac has days on record. Shortening to "one day and a restart" was the alternative; it was rejected because it would move most Macs on the first restart after the upgrade, before a scheduled job in another session had necessarily run once. **A login has no bar**: nothing that already ran can break, and the owner is present with the passphrase — where that is true: a new device, or one that depended on the enclave already (the review, item 5, took the `logout`-and-`login` in the middle of a trial out of it). And "three days" are three dates at least 48 hours apart (item 6).

**The objections of §17.28 and of its first review, and what became of them.**

| objection | now |
|---|---|
| "the one step that can lock a device out" | The move loses nothing by itself (the bytes are sealed, read back through the enclave and compared before the plain file goes; `use file` returns them). What it adds is a dependency on one Mac's enclave. The way back is `gclone login` with the passphrase, and every message of a sealed store that does not open says so. **Accepted risk**: an owner who has forgotten the passphrase, has no other connected device, and whose enclave key dies has lost the vault — on the plain file that device would have survived a logic-board replacement or a migration (§15). |
| F7 "notes nobody reads; the recovery path unchecked" | The automatic move does not check the passphrase and lists no keyfile: it must not need the network or a person. The note is owed until a terminal sees it. A login has just handled the passphrase. `keystore use enclave` still checks. **Accepted.** |
| F5 "an older binary is invisible" | Still invisible. gclone 0.4.0 and older on a scheduler's `PATH` say "not connected" from the day of the move. The README's upgrade notes and the note itself say so and name `gclone keystore use file`; gclone 0.5.0 is not affected. **Accepted.** |
| F4 "the trial proves less than claimed" | It claims what it records: days, another boot, the sessions that ran, no failure. A session that never ran during the trial is not covered and fails later with a text that names the remedy (§8.2 "The bar"). |
| F3 crash points | The same sequence; the automatic move finishes its own interrupted move at the next run (the crash table's new rows); a test for every stop point. |
| F6 the opt-out file | Unchanged: only `keystore use` writes `keystore.json`; the automatic paths never do, so "no choice" keeps meaning "the default". |

**Two defects of 0.5.0, fixed.**
- (a) *With `GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0` set and no terminal at the first run, the once-only note that older backups still hold `secrets.json` in plain was never owed and never shown.* `backup_note` returned at once when the trial was switched off, although the note is about backups; the exclusion attribute was set by then, so the note never became due again. The check is gone. Test: `tests/keystore.rs::the_backup_note_is_owed_and_shown_with_the_trial_switched_off` (it fails on 0.5.0: "the note is owed: [CACHEDIR.TAG, secrets.json, secrets.lock]").
- (b) *`gclone keystore use enclave` as the first command after a login (or after `keystore check`, which stores nothing) left a permanent warning "the secrets are sealed to a key that was made at the move … the trial's evidence belongs to another key".* The command picked a new key (no trial yet), then opened the vault — and that load took the trial's first step, with another key; the move closed that record. The command now takes the trial's step once before it picks the key (step 0 of §8.2 — as first built, by loading the secrets like every command, which the review's item 1 corrected), so the one key of the run is the trial's and the secrets'. Also: a move on a device without any trial record no longer creates an empty "moved" record. Test: `tests/keystore.rs::a_move_as_the_first_command_after_login_leaves_no_warning_about_another_key` (it fails on 0.5.0 with two different public halves).

**Other changes that came with it.** `Report` and `gclone keystore --json` gained `trial_disabled`; the status lines of §7.3; `gclone keystore` reports "ended: its key holds the secrets" from the two files also where a killed move left the record un-ended, and the first load afterwards ends it; the "trial complete: `gclone keystore use enclave`" note of 0.5.0 is gone (`notes.ready_ms` is no longer written); `trial::within` is the one bounded-wait helper for work nobody asked for (the step, a login's key, the move) — and since the review `seal::Bounded` bounds every single call into the enclave, whoever makes it; a login that settles a merged view says "… are one again" and, where it then seals, the line of §7.3.

**Deviations from the task as it was set**, each on purpose:
1. **"Any login that writes the secrets" seals — except a login on a device that was already working from a keyed `secrets.json`.** There the bar applies: a re-login (a renewed consent, say) must not be the moment a scheduled job in another session meets a store it cannot open. Such a device is moved by the trial, like every other.
2. **A login does not seal over a failure on this Mac's trial record** (unless the choice is `enclave`): a logout and login on a Mac whose scheduler's session failed the trial would otherwise break that scheduler.
3. **A login whose sealed file did not open writes a keyed `secrets.json` for the length of one command** before its end moves it (the keyless grant of a Drive login cannot take the place of sealed keys, §17.29 item 10, so the save table sends that login to the plain file first). "No plain file is left" holds at the end of the command, not at every instant of it.
4. **`GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0` also keeps a login from sealing** (unless the choice is `enclave`): "disables trial and automatic move" was read as "nothing unasked happens in this run". It is what the test harnesses of the other suites rely on. (After the review: "… on this device", once a run with it has used the plain file.)
5. **The automatic move tries the lock once** instead of waiting five seconds, and **is bounded at ten seconds** on its own thread; neither was asked for. A command must not wait for a step it did not ask for.
6. **The choice file is not written by the automatic paths** ("the same sequence" of `keystore use enclave` writes `enclave`): otherwise every Mac would read "the owner chose the sealed store", and the warning texts for that state would be about a command nobody ran.

**Review before the release: sixteen reports** (2026-11-14). Three reviewers ran the build above with the stand-in on a test clock, with the real Secure Enclave, with the released 0.4.0 and a 0.5.0 built from its commit, on a full disk, and with mutations of the code under the tests. Sixteen reports; two describe the same defect (8 and 13), so fifteen defects — every one confirmed again before it was touched, none rejected. Edited in place: §7.1, §7.3, §8.1, §8.2, §13 (item 8d), §15, this entry; `README.md` ("Status", "Upgrading to 0.5.1", "Publishing a release", "Where a device keeps its key", "Limitations", "Local files"), `docs/AUTH.md`, `scripts/release-sign-macos.sh`.
1. *`gclone keystore use enclave` checked nothing on a device whose trial had passed* (medium). Its step 0 loaded the secrets, and that load made the automatic move — before the key was proven against the vault and before the passphrase was checked; the command then said "already sealed … Nothing was moved", blamed "an interrupted `gclone keystore use file`", and exited 0 with a wrong passphrase. Step 0 is now the trial's step alone (`LayeredStore::without_unasked_move`); the command's own move follows its own checks on every device, onto the trial's key. On a device that is sealed already and has no choice on file the command says "keystore.json now records the sealed store as this device's choice." and nothing about an interrupted command. Test: `use_enclave_checks_the_passphrase_also_where_the_trial_has_passed` (exit 4, `secrets.json` byte for byte).
2. *A failure recorded when a login had to fall back was forgotten by the next trial* (medium). A device that the automatic move sealed broke in a session the trial had never seen; its owner signed in again from that session; the login could not seal there and wrote the reason into the ended record as `unavailable` — and `Record::begin` carried `unavailable` and failures over only from a record that never had a key. The new trial started clean, passed in the terminal, and broke the same session again. `Record::carried` now defines what a new trial inherits: everything on a record that never ended with a move; from one that did, `unavailable` (it can only have been written since) and the failures at or after `moved_ms`; `speaks_against` is the same question. Every moment of the record now comes from one clock (`trial::clock_ms`; the move used the wall clock beside the test clock). Tests: `trial::tests::a_new_trial_keeps_what_was_recorded_after_the_move`; `a_device_repaired_after_a_session_broke_it_is_not_moved_a_second_time`.
3. *`GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0` did the opposite of what the README promised for a scheduled job* (medium). Per process, the variable made the job's session invisible to the test; a terminal without it passed the bar and removed `secrets.json`; a job in a session that cannot use the enclave then failed with exit 4, and the record never held a failure although that session had run gclone every day. The variable now holds for the device: `keystore-trial.off` (§8.2). The README no longer says "does the same for that job's runs" of a variable that did not; it says what the marker does and what it cannot do for a job that carried the variable under 0.5.0. Tests: `the_environment_switch_keeps_the_plain_file_for_the_whole_device`, `a_job_that_sets_the_switch_is_not_broken_by_the_runs_that_do_not`, unit `the_marker_of_a_run_without_the_trial_keeps_the_plain_file_for_every_run`. The test harness's own devices set `GCLONE_TEST_KEYSTORE_NO_MARKER=1` beside the variable (§7.1), because they use it to prepare and to inspect devices, not to say anything about them.
4. *After the automatic move every command depended on an enclave call without a time bound* (medium). The step, the login's key and the move were bounded (§17.29 item 13); the open of a sealed store — in `load`, in `status` and `keystore`, and under the secrets lock in `save`, `keystore use file`, `settle_sealed` and the moves — was not. With the stand-in's `hang`, `ls`, `status` and `keystore` on a moved device were still running after 25 s, and a hung `keystore use file` kept the lock from a session that worked. `seal::Bounded` now wraps every sealer (`keystore::sealer`): ten seconds per call, then "the Secure Enclave did not answer within 10 s", and no second wait in that process. The text a command prints is the session text (exit 4; "Do not sign in again"; `gclone keystore use file` from a session where it works). Tests: `seal::tests::a_bounded_sealer_gives_up_on_a_call_that_does_not_return`, unit `a_sealed_store_whose_enclave_does_not_answer_is_an_error_not_a_standstill`, `a_sealed_device_whose_enclave_does_not_answer_fails_in_bounded_time` (five commands with a short bound through `GCLONE_TEST_KEYSTORE_WAIT_MS`, `ls` once with the real ten seconds).
5. *`gclone logout` and `gclone login` in the middle of a trial jumped the bar* (low). The save table's "neither file" row sealed at once to the trial's key unless the record held a failure — "2 of 3 days, no restart seen yet" became a sealed device, and a job in a session the trial had not reached failed with exit 4 instead of recording the failure that would have kept the plain file. A trial that is running and has not passed now holds a login back like a failure does (`LayeredStore::key_for_login`, `keystore::trial_undecided`, §8.2 "The bar"); a trial that has passed lends its key only where its test value opens. Tests: unit `a_login_in_the_middle_of_a_trial_stays_on_the_plain_file`; `a_logout_and_a_login_in_the_middle_of_a_trial_do_not_jump_its_bar`.
6. *"Three days" could be little more than one* (low): three UTC dates, no elapsed time — 23:59, 01:00 and 00:01 moved the secrets 1442 minutes after the trial began. Complete now needs the newest success to be 48 hours after the first (`last_ok_ms − created_ms ≥ trial::MIN_AGE_MS`, §8.2). Tests: `trial::tests::complete_needs_the_days_to_be_48_hours_apart`; `three_calendar_days_within_little_more_than_one_do_not_pass_the_trial`.
7. *The once-only note about the move could be lost for good* (low): on a disk with one free block the sealed file and the ended record were written, the marker was not, the plain file was removed all the same, and no later run said anything. The note is now a condition of the move (§8.2 "How"). Test: unit `the_automatic_move_does_not_happen_without_its_note`. (Not reproduced again on a full disk image: the unit test puts a directory where the marker goes.)
8. and 13. *A `gclone login` on a Mac whose trial record had ended left a permanent, false warning* (high) — defect (b) of this entry again, on two ordinary paths: `logout` and `login` on a device the automatic move had sealed, and the documented way back (the sealed key dead after a migration, then `login`). The ended record kept the public half of the old trial key; the login sealed to a key made then; `status` and `keystore` compared the two and warned, six days and a restart later too, that "the secrets are sealed to a key that was made at the move, not to the Secure Enclave trial's key (whose test value did not open at that moment)" — there had been no test value, and the key was made at a login. `trial::note_sealed` now ends a running trial and **forgets** the record of one that ended at an earlier sealing when another key takes the secrets (the save table's new store, and step (7) of every move); a blank record is "no trial" to `Report`. The warning stays for the one case it was made for — a trial that was running, with evidence, ended by a sealing to another key. Tests: `trial::tests::a_later_sealing_forgets_the_record_of_a_trial_that_ended_before`, unit `a_later_login_or_move_leaves_no_warning_about_the_ended_trial`, `a_login_or_a_move_after_the_automatic_move_leaves_no_warning_about_another_key` (logout and login; another Mac and login; `use file` and `use enclave`).
9. *An older gclone's sign-in after the move was undone three days later, again and again* (medium). 0.4.0 says "not connected", its owner signs in with it, a keyed `secrets.json` lies beside `secrets.sealed`; 0.5.1 started a new trial on it and its move accepted the old sealed file as "an interrupted move to finish". A sealed file beside the plain one is now the move's own unfinished work only if it is sealed to the running trial's key; anything else stops the trial and the move, and `status` says so (§8.2 "The trial", "Older binaries"). Tests: unit `an_older_logins_plain_file_beside_the_sealed_store_is_never_moved_again`; `an_older_gclones_login_beside_the_sealed_store_is_not_moved_again`; with the released 0.4.0, the last part of `the_released_0_4_0_binary_beside_the_new_files`.
10. *`status` and `keystore` promised a move that every run refused* (low): "trial complete: the next run … moves" beside a `secrets.sealed` that does not open or holds other keys, and a warning that offered `gclone keystore use file`, which refuses in that state without `--discard-sealed`. The line is now "kept: nothing is tested or moved while secrets.sealed lies beside it", `gclone keystore` says "complete, but nothing is moved while …", and the warning names `--discard-sealed` where the sealed file differs. Test: unit `the_status_line_and_warnings_for_every_state` (each kind of sealed file beside the plain one).
11. *The state that defect (b) had left on Macs that ran 0.5.0 stayed, with a clause that was false for it* (low). A record that ended on its first day without a restart is no evidence anybody could mistake: no warning, "none for the key that holds the secrets" in `gclone keystore`. The clause "(whose test value did not open at that moment)" is gone; the warning names `gclone keystore check --new-trial`, which on a sealed device now forgets the record and starts nothing (`trial::forget`) — it used to leave a running trial of a key that held nothing. Tests: unit `a_move_to_a_new_key_is_not_reported_as_the_trials_key`; `a_record_that_0_5_0_left_at_its_move_is_not_warned_about_for_good`.
12. *An owed note outlived the store it was about* (low): gclone 0.5.0 and 0.4.0 do not know `keystore-note.due`, their `logout` left it, and after a new login the next terminal run said "gclone tested it over several days and a restart first; the plain secrets.json is gone" about a store the login had just begun. The first save of a login on a signed-out device removes the marker, and so do the command and the move at the end of a login. Tests: unit `an_owed_move_note_does_not_outlive_the_store_it_is_about`; `a_note_that_an_older_logout_left_owed_is_not_shown_about_a_new_login`.
14. *The pre-publish gate never ran the 0.5.1 default, and this entry said it did* (medium). Step 10 of `scripts/release-sign-macos.sh` ran every command with `GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0`, which since 0.5.1 keeps a login from sealing: the one place where the signed binary runs on real hardware before a release made a plain-file login. It now takes the variable out of the environment, requires `secrets.sealed` and no `secrets.json` after the login wherever `keystore check` passes, and requires `keystore check` to have opened that sealed store; a machine without a Secure Enclave may skip in the self-test only, as before. The sentence under "Results" below is corrected.
15. *Five rules of §8.2 were pinned by no test* (medium; found by mutating the code): the opt-out re-check under the lock; the re-login that stays plain; the record ended after a move that was killed once the plain file had gone; the note not shown while `secrets.json` exists; `logout` removing the owed note. Each has an assertion now — unit `a_move_nobody_asked_for_looks_at_the_opt_outs_under_the_lock`; the last part of `a_logout_and_a_login_in_the_middle_of_a_trial_do_not_jump_its_bar` (a device without a trial record, where only `on_plain` stands between a re-login and the sealed store); `every_crash_point_of_the_automatic_move` (the record after every stop point; a reader with `GCLONE_TEST_NOTES=1` at the points where both files exist); `a_note_that_an_older_logout_left_owed_is_not_shown_about_a_new_login` — and each of the five mutations was applied again (the outcome is under "Results").
16. *The README said "a login seals from the start" without the exceptions* (low). Both places now say which logins seal (a Mac that is not connected, or whose sealed file no longer opens — and there "none is left at the end of the command", deviation 3) and which do not (signing in again on a Mac that works from the plain file; a `logout` and `login` during the test; after a recorded failure, until `--new-trial`).

**Results** (macOS 27.2, Apple silicon; cargo and rustc 1.99.0 from nix; Node 24.21; restic on `PATH` and `GCLONE_REQUIRE_RESTIC=1`; `GCLONE_REQUIRE_ENCLAVE=1`; `GCLONE_TEST_OLD_GCLONE` naming the released gclone 0.4.0 binary; `GCLONE_DEFAULT_AUTH_URL` unset). `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --locked` — **939 passed, 3 ignored** after the review (917 as first built, 895 before this entry: lib 433, `auth` 29, `backend_conformance` 37, `cli_e2e` 39, `cross_package` 14, `crypto_format` 41, `drive_http` 45, `index_adversary` 22, `index_props` 65, `keystore` 41, `restic_e2e` 26, `restic_http` 10, `sync_e2e` 55, `sync_faults` 16, `transfer` 42, `web` 24), the three hardware tests against the real Secure Enclave — whose sealer is now the bounded one — and the old-binary test among them (both seen to run, not skip, with `--nocapture`); `cargo build --release --locked`, without a warning. One run of the whole suite before the last one failed in `restic_e2e::restic_and_gclone_are_signalled_together` ("the lock was left behind … unable to create lock in backend: context canceled") — a race between restic's signal handling and gclone in a test whose harness switches the key store off; it passed six times alone, in the whole of `restic_e2e`, and in the final run, and nothing of this entry is in its path. The two regression tests of the defects were run against the unchanged 0.5.0 tree first: both failed there. `web-core/` (its manifest and lockfile carry the version): `cargo fmt --check`, clippy for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and for the host, `tests/parity.rs` 19, `web-core/build.sh` (the module's bytes change with the version string: 688,239 bytes), `web-core/test/run.sh` OK (without the browser smoke test). `worker/`: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` 56 + 239; the bundle built from that module, `check-dist` ok ("gclone viewer 0.5.1"), `npm run smoke` 375 checks, `npm run test:viewer` 45 — with the 0.5.1 release binary, whose temporary devices are now sealed by the real enclave. `tests/release/selftest.sh` with the 0.5.1 release binary and `GCLONE_REQUIRE_ENCLAVE=1`: 58 cases. (As first written this sentence said that its step 10 "runs a login, which now seals" — it did not: the script set `GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0`, review item 14. It does now, the self-test's first case requires the line "the login seals its secrets (secrets.sealed, no secrets.json)", and with the old line put back into the script the self-test fails at step 10.) **After the review**: `shellcheck` on the script and the self-test, `actionlint`; `web-core/` again (fmt, clippy for both targets, `tests/parity.rs` 19, `build.sh` with wasm-bindgen 0.2.130 — 688,239 bytes —, `test/run.sh` OK); `worker/`: `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` 56 (one skipped) + 239 — the viewer bundle, `check-dist`, `npm run smoke` and `npm run test:viewer` were **not** run again. **Mutations**: the five of review item 15 and eleven more, one per defect of the review that code decides (the load with the automatic move back in `use enclave`; `unavailable` after a move dropped; a foreign sealed file stepped over; an ended record kept; an undecided trial not holding a login; no age in "complete"; a marker that is no file counting as owed; a login keeping an older owed note; no `keystore-trial.off`; a begun trial counting as evidence; `blocked_by_sealed` never set) — each made one of the new tests fail, and the tree was compared with its state before. The reviewers' own scripts for items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 were run again against the new debug binary (their set-up lines given `GCLONE_TEST_KEYSTORE_NO_MARKER=1`): exit 4 and an untouched `secrets.json` for the wrong passphrase; "1 failure" and no second move after the repair; the job exits 0 on every day; `ls` and `status` exit 4 and `keystore` exits 0 after ten seconds; "2 of 3 days" after the logout and login; no move after 1442 minutes. **By hand, with release binaries and the real Secure Enclave**, in an isolated home under a temp directory: *0.5.1*, a first `login` (directory vault) — `secrets.sealed` with a 324-byte blob, no `secrets.json`, the line of §7.3; `copy`, `status`, `keystore`, `keystore check`, sixteen processes at once. *gclone 0.5.0 built from its commit, beside that store*: `ls`, `status` and `keystore` work. *A device made by 0.5.0* (plain file; its trial record holds a real enclave key): 0.5.1 continues that record ("1 of 3 days"); with the record edited by hand to three days and another boot — nothing else can age it in a release build — the next `gclone ls` of 0.5.1 moved the secrets to the 0.5.0 trial's key, owed the note (no terminal), and `gclone keystore` read "ended: its key holds the secrets (3 days, a restart survived)"; 0.5.0 then read the sealed store; the released 0.4.0 said "not connected (signed out)"; `keystore use file` gave back `secrets.json` byte for byte as 0.5.0 had written it, and 0.4.0 worked again. *A sealed file whose blob was damaged by one character*: the text of §2.8, exit 4; a `login` with a wrong passphrase left the file as it was; one with the passphrase ended sealed again. *`GCLONE_KEYSTORE_TRIAL=0`*: a login stayed on the plain file, and `status` said why. Everything was in that directory, which was removed; the enclave keys are not permanent, so nothing of them exists outside it.

**Not verified.** **Of the review's fixes:** the ten-second bound was never exercised by a real framework call that blocks (nobody has seen one) — only by the stand-in's `hang`, and by the real enclave answering in time; a thread left inside Security.framework until the process ends is assumed to be harmless there. The full-disk case of item 7 was not repeated on a disk image. `keystore-trial.off` was not tried under a real scheduler, and it cannot help a job that carried the variable under 0.5.0 before that job's first run with this version (§15). The signed binary's sealing login in step 10 ran with an ad hoc signature in the self-test, not yet with the Developer ID. gclone 0.5.0 (built from its commit) beside the files this version now writes was run once by hand with the real enclave, in a lab that was removed afterwards — a 0.5.0 device continued by 0.5.1 (`last_ok_ms` in the record), the marker `keystore-trial.off`, a store sealed by 0.5.1's `use enclave`, and a forgotten record after a `logout` and `login`: `ls`, `status` and `keystore` of 0.5.0 worked each time — and is in no test. **Time and real machines.** No Mac has gone through the real thing: three calendar days, a real restart, and the move by a real scheduled job — the bar was passed on the test clock (the stand-in, and once with a real enclave key) and by editing a record by hand. A sealed file across a real restart or a macOS update is still unmeasured (§17.28); on a device that was on the plain file the trial now measures the restart before anything depends on it, **a fresh login depends on it unmeasured**. ssh, a LaunchDaemon, `user/<uid>` agents, a locked screen, FileVault off before the first login: not run; gclone's own binary from cron and from a LaunchAgent: not run (the experiments of §17.28 measured a probe binary there). A Mac without a Secure Enclave, a virtual machine, a hosted CI runner: only the stand-in's "no key can be made" and "does not return" paths ran — that the real framework answers with an error there, within the two seconds a login waits, is an expectation. A real migration to another Mac or a restore from a backup: the "dead key" text was produced with the stand-in's other machine and with a damaged blob, not by moving files between two Macs. The note about the move and the login's line were seen through the test switch and in captured output, never on a real terminal. **Older and newer binaries.** gclone 0.5.0 beside a sealed store was run by hand, not in a test (no test builds another version); 0.4.0 was run by the test and by hand, the macOS build only. A long-running `gclone web` or `serve restic` of 0.4.0 or 0.5.0 across an automatic move was not run. **Linux.** Nothing of this entry was compiled or run on Linux (no container and no Linux target were at hand): the change has no code under a platform `cfg` of its own and no sealer exists there, so "nothing changes on Linux" is an expectation that CI has to show — `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `tests/keystore.rs`, whose new tests use the stand-in and are expected to pass there. `tests/install/test.sh`, the browser suites and the viewer's e2e tests were not run again (nothing they cover changed but the version string). Nothing ran against GitHub, Google Drive or a deployed Worker.

### 17.31 The README is a product page; its sections moved (2026-11-14)

No behaviour changed. `README.md` had grown to some 1,900 lines of setup, reference, security model and release procedure. It is now a short product page (what gclone is, install, quick start, features with screenshots, the security model and the limitations in brief), and what it held is in four documents, **under the headings it had**:

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/USAGE.md` | "Installing and updating" (the installer's checks and options, updating), "Commands" with "How `copy` and `sync` behave" and its siblings, "Browse the vault in your browser", "Browse from any browser (the hosted viewer)", "Back up with restic", "Using a vault without Google", "Local files", "Exit codes", "Limitations" |
| `docs/SETUP.md` | "One-time setup" (in short; `worker/README.md` stays the authoritative version), the first device, "Adding a device", "Day-0 checklist (before the first real use)" (§2.9) |
| `docs/SECURITY.md` | "Security model", "The hosted viewer: what you trust" (the "What you trust", phishing-habits and password-manager paragraphs of the old hosted-viewer section), "Where a device keeps its key" with "Upgrading a Mac to 0.5.1", "Lost or stolen device", "If a passphrase or a device's key file leaked", "After a change of hands (the hosted viewer)" |
| `DEVELOPMENT.md` | "Building" (was "Building from source"), "Tests" and "CI" (was "Development"), "Screenshots" (new: `worker/test/e2e/readme/`, `docs/images/`), "Publishing a release", "Repository layout" |

The "Status" section is gone: what it said about what has and has not run against the real services is the first entry of "Limitations". **Entries §17.1–§17.30 name sections of `README.md` as it was when they were written**; read them with this table. References in the body of this spec (§1.3, §2.8, §2.9, §7, §8, §13–§15), in `docs/AUTH.md`, in `worker/README.md` and in the comments of the code name the new places.

Two texts changed with it. `gclone passwd`'s closing warning ends "…see "If a passphrase or a device's key file leaked" in docs/SECURITY.md." (§2.8, §7.2; it said "in the README" — the binaries of 0.5.0 and 0.5.1 still do, so the README's "No re-keying" entry links that section under its name), and `scripts/release-sign-macos.sh` names `DEVELOPMENT.md` in its keychain warning and in `--help`. `install.sh` still says "(README, "Building from source")": the README keeps a section of that name. The documents now say that `--json` is also accepted by `gclone keystore` without a subcommand (§7.3), which the README had left out.
